15	NCOR complex	NCOR1 complex	Human	HeLa cells	12628926	Corepressors N-CoR and SMRT participate in diverse repression pathways and exist in large protein complexes including HDAC3, TBL1 and TBLR1. The purified N-CoR complex contains 10-12 associated proteins, including previously identified components and a novel actin-binding protein IR10. It is shown that TBL1/TBLR1 associates with N-CoR through two independent interactions: the N-terminal region and the C-terminal WD-40 repeats interact with the N-CoR RD1 and RD4 region, respectively. In vitro, TBL1/TBLR1 bind histones H2B and H4, and, importantly, repression by TBL1/TBLR1 correlates with their interaction with histones. By using specific small interference RNAs (siRNAs), the authors demonstrate that HDAC3 is essential, whereas TBL1 and TBLR1 are functionally redundant but essential for repression by unliganded thyroid hormone receptor. 181	26S proteasome		Human	HeLa cells	11812135	The proteasome is an essential component of the ATP-dependent proteolytic pathway in eukaryotic cells and is responsible for the degradation of most cellular proteins (for reviews see PMID:8811196 and PMID:10872471). It contains a barrel-shaped proteolytic core complex (the 20S proteasome), and is capped at one or both ends by regulatory complexes like the 19S complex (PMID:11812135), modulator (PMID:8621709), PA28 (PMID:9325261) and PA28gamma (PMID:9325261). Interferon-gamma (IFN-gamma) alters the peptide-degrading specificity of proteasomes and produces an immunoproteasome responsible for accelerated processing of nonself endogenous antigens by inducing the replacement of subunits Psmb5, Psmb6 and Psmb7 by Psmb8, Psmb9 and Psmb10, respectively.			In tumor xenografts of living mice, it was shown that bortezomib blocks 26S proteasome function (PMID: 12819780). In a study, it was shown that carfilzomib inhibits the 26S proteasome in peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PMID: 33589757). In a study, it was shown that ixazomib inhibits the 26S proteasome in MDA-MB-468 human breast adenocarcinoma cells (PMID: 31754034). 192	PA28-20S proteasome	11S-20S proteasome	Human	blood	11676531	The proteasome is an essential component of the ATP-dependent proteolytic pathway in eukaryotic cells and is responsible for the degradation of most cellular proteins (for reviews see PMID:8811196 and PMID:10872471). 229	NAT complex		Human		9734358	A complex, NAT, that represses activation of transcription by RNAPII has been isolated. The NAT complex is composed of approximately 20 polypeptides and includes a subset of the Srb polypeptides, hSrb7, hSrb10, and hSrb11, as well as hRgr1 and hMed6. The presence of hSrb10, hSrb11, and hRgr1 in a complex that functions to down-regulate transcription is consistent with studies in yeast demonstrating that Srb8-Srb11, as well as Rgr1, function as negative regulators of transcription in vivo. It has been suggested that the NAT complex is a subcomplex of the RNAPII holoenzyme and its function and regulation is through the RNAPII holoenzyme. 230	Mediator complex	Mediator of transcriptional regulation	Human		15175163	Regulation of transcription by RNA polymerase II (Pol II) is controlled by specific combinations of sequence-specific, DNA binding regulatory transcription factors (TFs) bound to a gene's promoter and enhancer regions. These TFs interact with several multiprotein complexes that remodel the chromatin context of the promoter, integrate signals from multiple TFs to control the frequency of transcription initiation, and regulate the efficiency of transcription elongation. One such complex is the Mediator, an ~2-megadalton complex of 20 to 30 subunits that is believed to function as a molecular bridge by simultaneously interacting with both DNA-bound TFs and Pol II. Several identical subunits appear in protein complexes like DRIP/ARC, CRSP, NAT, PC2, SMCC and Mediator, indicating that unique classes of transcription activators may share common sets or subsets of cofactors. 860	DNMT1-EHMT2-PCNA complex	DNMT1-G9a-PCNA complex	Human	HeLa cells, HEK293 cells	17085482	DNMT1 and G9a are loaded onto the chromatin simultaneously in a ternary complex with loading factor PCNA during chromatin replication. Zebularine is a DNMT1-specific mechanistic inhibitor (PMID: 17085482). The two DNMT inhibitors azacitidine (5-Aza) and decitabine are hypomethylating agents (HMAs) currently approved for clinical use (PMID: 29301553). They are the most commonly used nucleoside agents in cancer. After cellular uptake, the first limiting step is the ATP-dependent phosphorylation of nucleosides to form monophosphorylated nucleotides. These monophosphorylated nucleotides are incorporated into DNA in the place of cytosine. Then, DNMTs recognize the azacytosine-guanine dinucleotide and catalyze the methylation reaction by forming a covalent bond with the cytosine ring. The covalent complex at C6 cannot be resolved through b-elimination, because of the presence of a nitrogen atom at position 5. Covalently trapped DNMTs are degraded, resulting in the depletion of cellular DNMTs (PMID: 34452630). 898	Mediator complex 1	High-molecular-mass Mediator complex 1; 2MDa Mediator complex 1	Human		11416138	Regulation of transcription by RNA polymerase II (Pol II) is controlled by specific combinations of sequence-specific, DNA binding regulatory transcription factors (TFs) bound to a gene's promoter and enhancer regions. These TFs interact with several multiprotein complexes that remodel the chromatin context of the promoter, integrate signals from multiple TFs to control the frequency of transcription initiation, and regulate the efficiency of transcription elongation. One such complex is the Mediator, an ~2-megadalton complex of 20 to 30 subunits that is believed to function as a molecular bridge by simultaneously interacting with both DNA-bound TFs and Pol II. Several identical subunits appear in protein complexes like DRIP/ARC, CRSP, NAT, PC2, SMCC and Mediator, indicating that unique classes of transcription activators may share common sets or subsets of cofactors. 1174	PHAX-CBC complex (cap binding complex)		Human		10786834	In metazoa, assembly of spliceosomal U snRNPs requires nuclear export of U snRNA precursors. 1250	RB1-E2F1 complex		Human	MCF7 cells	17380128	The phosphorylation of pRB at Ser612 is induced by ATM-Chk1/2 kinase after DNA damage, leading to enhancement of the formation of a complex between pRB and E2F-1. It is proposed, that in asynchronously growing cells, pRB exists in a predominantly phosphorylated state, which is dissociated from E2F, allowing E2F-dependent transcription. DNA damage induces dephosphorylation of pRB at Cdk phosphorylation sites, leading to the complex pRB-E2F-1 being formed. 1300	CALCRL-RAMP1 complex	CRLR-RAMP1 complex	Human	HEK 293T cells	11387328	"The results demonstrate that RAMP2 and RAMP3 and not only RAMP1 can promote the full maturation of CRLR, leading to its terminal glycosylation, and only the fully processed receptors were found to bind AM (adrenomedullin) and CGRP (calcitonin gene-related peptide) (PMID: 11387328).

"Calcitonin gene-related peptide (CGRP) is involved in migraine pathophysiology. CGRP can signal through two receptors. The canonical CGRP receptor comprises the calcitonin receptor-like receptor and receptor activity-modifying protein 1 (RAMP1); the AMY1 receptor comprises the calcitonin receptor with RAMP1. Drugs that reduce CGRP activity, such as receptor antagonists, are approved for the treatment and prevention of migraine. Erenumab antagonised both the CGRP and AMY1 receptors with an 20-120-fold preference for the CGRP receptor, depending on the cells, agonist, analytical approach and/or assay format. Erenumab antagonised both forms of CGRP equally, and appeared to act as a competitive reversible antagonist at both receptors (PMID: 37580864).
The FDA approved ubrogepant and rimegepant as oral drugs to treat migraines by targeting the calcitonin-gene related peptide receptor (CGRPR). Ubrogepant and Rimegepant are CGRPR antagonists (PMID: 34184869).
Orally administered next-generation small molecule calcitonin-gene related peptide receptor antagonists have been shown to have safety and efficacy in acute treatment (ubrogepant and rimegepant) and prevention (atogepant) of migraine, giving additional CGRP-based therapeutic options for migraine patients (PMID: 31020659).
A significant trigger in migraine pathophysiology is calcitonin gene-related peptide (CGRP). Several drugs, such as gepants and monoclonal antibodies (MABs) targeting CGRP or its receptor, have been developed to antagonize CGRP signaling. Zavegepant (Zavzpret), a CGRP receptor antagonist, has been approved by the FDA for the acute treatment of migraine (PMID: 38333255).

The covalent complex at C6 cannot be resolved through b-elimination, because of the presence of a nitrogen atom at position 5. Covalently trapped DNMTs are degraded, resulting in the depletion of cellular DNMTs (PMID: 34452630). Zebularine is a DNMT1-specific mechanistic inhibitor (PMID: 17085482). 2003	COX1 complex	PTGS1 complex	Human	ram seminal vesicles	11318639	Two isoforms of prostaglandin endoperoxide H synthases are found in mammals: the constitutively expressed PTGS1 and the inducible PTGS2. Both enzymes are present on the lumenal surfaces of the ER and of the inner and outer membranes of the nuclear envelope.		Inhibition of COX confers relief from inflammatory, pyretic, thrombotic, neurodegenerative and oncological maladies.	In a human whole blood assay, it was shown that the nonsteroid anti-inflammatory drugs aspirin, diclofenac, diflunisal, fenoprofen, flufenamic acid, flurbiprofen, ibuprofen, indomethacin, ketoprofen, ketorolac, meclofenamic acid, mefenamic acid, naproxen, aminosalicylic acid (=mesalazine; Olsalazine is a prodrug of mesalazine), piroxicam, sulfasalazine and tolmetin inhibit the activity of the PTGS1 (COX-1) complex (PMID: 10377455). In a study it was shown, that in leucocytes acemetacin inhibits the activity of the PTGS1 complex more potently than in gastric mucosa (PMID: 8144313). In an animal model, it was shown that bromfenac was approximately 32 times more active against PTGS2 complex than PTGS1 complex (PMID: 16846546). In rat adjuvant-induced arthritis (AIA) model, it was shown that felbinac and loxoprofen inhibit the activity of the PTGS1 complex and the PTGS2 complex (PMID: 27241582). In a study with Thai healthy volunteers, it was shown that floctafenine inhibits the activity of the PTGS1 complex and the PTGS2 complex (PMID: 23755755). In the eye, nepafenac is converted to an active metabolite, amfenac, which like nepafenac is a reversible inhibitor of the PTGS1 complex and the PTGS2 complex (PMID: 19897019). In vitro studies on the two isoforms of COX enzyme, performed on human platelets and human synovial fluid cells, demonstrated that oxaprozin inhibits the PTGS1 complex and the PTGS2 complex (PMID: 15324530). After demonstrating that tiaprofenic acid (RMD86) presents in vivo antinociceptive and antipyretic effects, a molecular docking was shown for two enzymes greatly involved in inflammatory processes, the PTGS1 complex and the PTGS2 complex (PMID: 33294672). In a whole blood assay from healthy volunteers, it was shown that bismuth subsalicylate inhibits the activity of the PTGS1 complex and the PTGS2 complex (PMID: 9626023). 2649	DNMT3A-MYC-ZBTB17 complex		Human	HeLa nuclear extract, U2OS cells	15616584	This complex is involved in a transcriptional silencing of p21Cip1 promoter. Myc represses transcription through recruitment of DNA methyltransferase corepressor (PMID: 15616584).			The two DNMT inhibitors azacitidine (5-Aza) and decitabine are hypomethylating agents (HMAs) currently approved for clinical use (PMID: 29301553). They are the most commonly used nucleoside agents in cancer. After cellular uptake, the first limiting step is the ATP-dependent phosphorylation of nucleosides to form monophosphorylated nucleotides. These monophosphorylated nucleotides are incorporated into DNA in the place of cytosine. Then, DNMTs recognize the azacytosine-guanine dinucleotide and catalyze the methylation reaction by forming a covalent bond with the cytosine ring. The covalent complex at C6 cannot be resolved through b-elimination, because of the presence of a nitrogen atom at position 5. Covalently trapped DNMTs are degraded, resulting in the depletion of cellular DNMTs (PMID: 34452630). 3133	PIK3CA-PIK3R1 complex	Phosphatidylinositol 3-kinase (PIK3CA, PIK3R1)	Human		18079394	Phosphatidylinositol 3-kinases (PI3Ks) are lipid kinases that phosphorylate phosphatidylinositol 4,5-bisphosphate at the 3-position of the inositol ring, and thus generate phosphatidylinositol 3,4,5-trisphosphate (PIP3 ), which, in turn, initiates a vast array of signaling events. PI3Ks are heterodimers, composed of catalytic and regulatory subunits, that are activated by growth factor-receptor tyrosine kinases (PMID: 18079394).	Class IA phosphoinositide 3-kinases (PI3Ks) are obligate catalytic p110 and regulatory p85 heterodimers. These heterodimers consist of a p110 catalytic subunit (p110alpha/PIK3CA, p110beta/PIK3CB, or p110delta/PIK3CD) bound to any of the distinct regulatory subunits (p85alpha/PIK3R1, p85beta/PIK3R2, or p55/PIK3R3) (PMID: 17470792).	PIK3CA mutations are involved in breast cancer (PMID: 31091374), but also in different other types of cancer. Defects in the phosphatidylinositol 3-kinase pathway contribute to type II diabetes (PMID: 18079394).	Copanlisib inhibits the catalytic activity of all four PI3Kisoforms (P110alpha, P110beta, P110delta, and P110gamma), with the highest selectivity for the PI3Kalpha and PI3Kdelta isoforms. These isoforms are commonly found in malignant B cells, namely chronic lymphocytic lymphoma (CLL) and diffuse large B cell lymphoma (DLBCL) (PMID: 33889376). Alpelisib (BYL719) is an orally bioavailable, small-molecule, alpha-specific PI3K inhibitor that selectively inhibits p110alpha approximately 50 times as strongly as other isoforms. The combination of alpelisib with fulvestrant had synergistic antitumor activity (PMID: 31091374).	"[PIK3CA; PIK3CA-PIK3R1 complex; 3133; copanlisib; inhibits; complex activity; 33889376]

3830	Beta-2 adrenergic receptor	ADRB2 homodimer	Human	HEK293 cells 	17363375				"Nadolol, penbutolol, pindolol, propranolol, and timolol are non-selective first generation beta-blockers (PMID: 31809852).
Carteolol, carvedilol, and labetalol are non-selective third generation beta-blockers (PMID: 31809852).
Metipranolol and levobunolol are non-cardio-selective beta-adrenoceptor antagonists (PMID: 2883990).
Bupranolol is a beta1- and beta2-blocking drug with some intrinsic sympathomimetic and local anesthetic activity (PMID: 3951800).
Sotalol, timolol, propranolol, and carvedilol are nonselective beta-blockers (PMID: 37885367).
The inotropic activity of dobutamine has previously been attributed to selective stimulation of myocardial beta 1-adrenoceptors. However, recent studies from a number of laboratories indicate that the mechanism of action of dobutamine is substantially more complex. Dobutamine has the capacity to stimulate beta 1-, beta 2-, and alpha 1-adrenoceptors in the cardiovascular system at doses that approximate those used clinically. It has recently been suggested that the inotropic activity of dobutamine results from combined beta 1- and alpha 1-adrenoceptor stimulation in the myocardium, and that this activity could explain, at least in part, the inotropic selectivity of the compound (PMID: 3310640).
Epinephrine and norepinephrine are non-selective adrenic receptor agonists, their actions result from the activation of nine different adrenoreceptors (PMID: 30740663).
L-threo-3,4-dihydroxyphenylserine (L-DOPS, droxidopa) is a synthetic catecholamino acid. When taken orally, L-DOPS is converted to the sympathetic neurotransmitter, norepinephrine (NE), via decarboxylation catalyzed by L-aromatic-amino-acid decarboxylase (LAAAD) (PMID: 17214596).
Isoprenaline is a non-selective beta-receptor agonist, lacking alpha-agonist effect (PMID: 27919274).
Salbutamol, formoterol, ritodrine, salmeterol, terbutaline, and tulobuterol are beta2-specific agonists (PMID: 20590599).
Bitolterol is a beta-adrenoceptor agonist which is hydrolysed to colterol by tissue esterases present at high concentrations in the lung. Animal studies indicate that bitolterol has significant beta2-selectivity (PMID: 3278878).
Ephedrine is a beta2-agonist (PMID: 16750469).
Levosalbutamol is a chirally pure beta2-adrenoceptor agonist developed from racemic salbutamol (PMID: 18031154).
The beta2-adrenoceptor agonist bronchodilators terbutaline and orciprenaline are also weak alpha1-adrenoceptor antagonists (PMID: 32592771).
The beta1 and beta2 antagonists pindolol and oxprenolol are agonists of the beta3 adrenoreceptor (PMID: 1309479).
The short-acting beta2 adrenergic drugs most frequently used include albuterol, pirbuterol, and levalbuterol (PMID: 17594727).
Reproterol (a selective beta2-adrenoceptor agonist with a theophylline moiety) exerts anti-inflammatory actions through inhibition of cyclic AMP (cAMP) PDE activity (PMID: 15219266).
Indacaterol is an inhaled beta2-adrenoceptor agonist with a 24-h duration of action (PMID: 16434564).
Indacaterol, olodaterol, vilanterol, and carmoterol are called ultra long-acting beta2-adrenoceptor agonists (PMID: 21232045).
Arformoterol (R,R-formoterol) is a single isomer form of the beta2-adrenoceptor agonist formoterol. This isomer contains two chiral centres developed as an inhaled preparation for the treatment of respiratory disorders (PMID: 14725487).

5412	5-hydroxytryptamine receptor 1D	HTR1D  homodimer	Human	HEK-293 cells	11854302				"Vortioxetine, an antidepressant for the treatment of major depressive disorder (MDD), is a 5-HT3, 5-HT7 and 5-HT1D receptor antagonist, 5-HT1B receptor partial agonist, 5-HT1A receptor agonist and serotonin (5-HT) transporter (SERT) inhibitor (PMID: 25016186).
Almotriptan, is a 5-HT1B/1D-receptor agonist used to treat migraine (PMID: 10824628).
Sumatriptan and eletriptan are 5-HT 1B/1D agonists for the treatment of migraine attacks (PMID: 11221281).
Frovatriptan is a 5-hydroxytryptamine (5-HT)(1B/1D) agonist (PMID: 12028322).
The advent of the triptans revolutionized acute migraine treatment. The older migraine-specific drugs, the ergot alkaloids (ergotamine and dihydroergotamine), also relieve migraine attacks through agonism at the 5-HT1B and 5-HT1D receptors, but the triptans have much greater specificity for these receptors. Unlike the ergot alkaloids, the triptans do not activate many other receptor types, and therefore are much better tolerated. This reduction in side effects greatly enhanced their clinical utility as it allowed a far greater proportion of patients to take a full therapeutic dose. There is extensive evidence that the seven triptans: sumatriptan, zolmitriptan, rizatriptan, eletriptan, naratriptan, almotriptan, and frovatriptan, are effective in the acute treatment of migraine (PMID: 38307644)." 5421	5-hydroxytryptamine receptor 1A	HTR1A homodimer	Human	HEK-293 cells	11854302	The 5-hydroxytryptamine receptor 1A (5-HT1A) is known to activate a variety of effectors via G i/o proteins, and receptor stimulation leads to inhibition of adenylyl cyclase (AC). The 5-HT1A receptor is also involved in G-beta-gamma-mediated activation of a K+ current, inhibition of a Ca 2+ current, and stimulation of the phospholipase C, as well as an activation of the mitogen-activated protein kinase Erk2. One important mechanism regulating 5-HT1A receptor function is receptor desensitization and internalization. 5-HT1A receptor activation leads to effective internalization of 5-HT1A autoreceptors in the nucleus raphe dorsalis, but not of heteroreceptors resided in hippocampal neurons, indicating the difference in the regulation of pre- and postsynaptic 5-HT1A receptors activity (PMID: 24935787).		"The 5-hydroxytryptamine receptor 1A (5-HT1A) is known to be critically involved in major depression, anxiety, and suicide. Several rare single-nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) were described for 5-HT1A receptor gene. Between those, the SNP C(-1019)G localized in the repressor region of promoter is of
particular interest because of its association with depression, suicidal behavior, and schizophrenia as well as sensitivity to the antidepressant drug treatment (PMID: 24935787)."	"The antipsychotic aripiprazole is a potent, partial agonist at the human 5-HT1A receptor (PMID: 12063084).
Buspirone acts as a partial agonist at the postsynaptic 5HT1A receptor and a full agonist at presynaptic 5HT1A receptors (PMID: 16272182).
Vilazodone is a combined serotonin specific reuptake inhibitor (SSRI) and 5-HT1A receptor partial agonist for the treatment of affective disorders (PMID: 19499624).
Vortioxetine, an antidepressant for the treatment of major depressive disorder (MDD), is a 5-HT3, 5-HT7 and 5-HT1D receptor antagonist, 5-HT1B receptor partial agonist, 5-HT1A receptor agonist and serotonin (5-HT) transporter (SERT) inhibitor (PMID: 25016186).
Brexpiprazole is an oral atypical antipsychotic agent approved for the treatment of schizophrenia in the EU (in adult patients) and the USA, as well as in some other countries, including Japan. Like aripiprazole, it is a partial agonist at dopamine D2 and serotonin 5-HT1A receptors and an antagonist at serotonin 5-HT2A receptors (PMID: 30671869).
At clinically relevant doses, flibanserin acts predominantly at 5-HT(1A) receptors as an agonist and secondarily at 5-HT(2A) receptors as an antagonist (PMID: 20840530).
Cariprazine is a dopamine D3 and D2 receptor partial agonist, with a preference for the D3 receptor. Cariprazine is also a partial agonist at the serotonin 5-HT1A receptor and acts as an antagonist at 5-HT2B and 5-HT2A receptors (PMID: 27440212).
Aripiprazole lauroxil is a long-acting intramuscular injection that works as a combination of partial agonist activity at D2 and 5-HT1A receptors combined with antagonist activity at 5-HT2A receptors (PMID: 34287335)." 5691	TNFSF13B homooligomer	TALL1 homooligomer; BAFF homooligomer	Human	in vitro	14749821	TNFSF13B (BAFF; TALL1) is produced as a membrane-bound protein containing a TNF homologous extracellular domain which is responsible for trimer formation. Upon proteolytic cleavage it is released as a soluble ligand, which exists either as trimer or 60-mer that results from the ordered assembly of twenty trimers (PMID: 31380267; 33240880; 12796483). TNFSF13B (BAFF; TALL1) is active as homotrimer under normal physiological conditions. It is discussed, that the formation of higher-order oligomers is an artefact of tagging the amino terminus of the protein with a histidine tag (PMID: 14749821).		BAFF regulates homeostasis of peripheral B cells and is elevated in the circulation of patients with autoimmune diseases such as systemic lupus erythematosus (PMID: 30524439). 5693	BAZ2A-DNMT1-DNMT3B-HDAC1-SMARCA5 complex	TIP5-DNMT-HDAC1 complex	Human	HEK293T cells	16085498	The PHD finger/bromodomain of TIP5 interacts with HDAC1, DNMT1, DNMT3b, and SNF2h and triggers histone deacetylation and rDNA methylation (PMID: 16085498).			The two DNMT inhibitors azacitidine (5-Aza) and decitabine are hypomethylating agents (HMAs) currently approved for clinical use (PMID: 29301553). They are the most commonly used nucleoside agents in cancer. After cellular uptake, the first limiting step is the ATP-dependent phosphorylation of nucleosides to form monophosphorylated nucleotides. These monophosphorylated nucleotides are incorporated into DNA in the place of cytosine. Then, DNMTs recognize the azacytosine-guanine dinucleotide and catalyze the methylation reaction by forming a covalent bond with the cytosine ring. The covalent complex at C6 cannot be resolved through b-elimination, because of the presence of a nitrogen atom at position 5. Covalently trapped DNMTs are degraded, resulting in the depletion of cellular DNMTs (PMID: 34452630). Trichostatin A (TSA) or aza-deoxycytidine (aza-dC) are inhibitors of histone deacetylases and DNA methyltransferases (PMID: 16085498). Zebularine is a DNMT1-specific mechanistic inhibitor (PMID: 17085482). 6137	GM-CSF receptor complex	CSF2-CSF2RA-CSF2RB ternary complex	Human	erythroleukemic TF-1 cell line	18692472	Granulocyte-macrophage colony-stimulating factor (GM-CSF) is a pleiotropic cytokine that controls the production and function of blood cells. It is deregulated in clinical conditions such as rheumatoid arthritis and leukemia. Its receptors are heterodimers consisting of a ligand-specific alpha subunit and a beta subunit that is shared with the interleukin (IL)-3 and IL-5 receptors. JAK2 activation is a feature of GM-CSF receptor activation and plays a critical  role in GM-CSF signaling. The structure of the GM-CSF receptor complex reveals a hexameric 2:2:2 assembly, consisting of two beta chains, two GMR alpha chains, and two GM-CSF molecules. The crystal lattice generates an unexpected dodecamer complex, an assembly consisting of two hexameric complexes related by a crystallographic two-fold axis. The dodecamer assembles in a head-to-head orientation. Functional studies reveal that dodecamer formation is required for receptor activation and signaling. This differs from the 2:1:1 stoichiometry  (2 betac,1 GMRalpha,1 GM-CSF) (McClure et al., 2003). This is likely to be a result of differences in the total protein concentration at which the complex is formed as we observe a protein concentration-dependent shift in molecular  weight and hence stoichiometry of GM-CSF receptor complex. The 2:1:1 complex probably represents a relatively stable intermediate in the assembly of higher-order 2:2:2 GM-CSFreceptor complexes.		Abnormalities in GM-CSF production or receptor function have been implicated in multiple pathologies such as rheumatoid arthritis (Cook et al., 2001), juvenile myelomonocytic leukemia (Birnbaum et al., 2000), chronic myelomonocytic leukemia (Ramshaw et al., 2002), and alveolar proteinosis (Dirksen et al., 1998). Furthermore, the GM-CSF receptor may also be important in the pathogenesis of chronic myeloid leukemia and myeloproliferative diseases by propagating survival and proliferation signalspromoted by the abnormal expression of Bcr-Abl and JAK2 mutations, respectively (PMID:18692472).	Sargramostim is a yeast-derived recombinant human granulocyte-macrophage colony stimulating factor (GM-CSF) that enhances neutrophil recovery and myeloid engraftment and is mainly used to treat neutropenia (PMID: 9377627). Binding of sargramostim to CSF2RA induces dimerization of CSF2RA with the CSF2RAB subunit of the receptor complex leading to activation of a Janus kinase (JAK2) (PMID: 9845514). Binding of sargramostim to CSF2RB is only indirect. 6336	CTNNB1-DNMT1 complex		Human	HC-116 cells; HEK293 cells	25753001	The protein interaction between beta-Catenin and DNMT1 regulates Wnt signaling and DNA methylation in colorectal cancer cells (PMID: 25753001).		Colorectal cancer (PMID: 25753001).	The two DNMT inhibitors azacitidine (5-Aza) and decitabine are hypomethylating agents (HMAs) currently approved for clinical use (PMID: 29301553). They are the most commonly used nucleoside agents in cancer. After cellular uptake, the first limiting step is the ATP-dependent phosphorylation of nucleosides to form monophosphorylated nucleotides. These monophosphorylated nucleotides are incorporated into DNA in the place of cytosine. Then, DNMTs recognize the azacytosine-guanine dinucleotide and catalyze the methylation reaction by forming a covalent bond with the cytosine ring. The covalent complex at C6 cannot be resolved through b-elimination, because of the presence of a nitrogen atom at position 5. Covalently trapped DNMTs are degraded, resulting in the depletion of cellular DNMTs. Decitabine can decrease DNMT1 and DNMT3A expression, reversing abnormal transcription activation, while azacitidine only targets DNMT1 (PMID: 34452630, 37345101). Zebularine is a DNMT1-specific mechanistic inhibitor (PMID: 17085482).	"[DNMT1; CTNNB1-DNMT1 complex; 6336; decitabine; inhibits; complex formation; 34452630]

6345	ZNF304-corepressor complex		Human	DLD-1 cells	24623306	Promoter-bound ZNF304 recruits a corepressor complex that includes the DNA methyltransferase DNMT1, resulting in DNAhypermethylation and transcriptional silencing.		The ZNF304-corepressor complex is involved in colorectal cancer. ZNF304 is a protein that binds to stretches of DNA, including regions of DNA at the start of several tumor suppressor genes, and it recruits the enzymes that add the chemical marks that switch off these genes.	The two DNMT inhibitors azacitidine (5-Aza) and decitabine are hypomethylating agents (HMAs) currently approved for clinical use (PMID: 29301553). They are the most commonly used nucleoside agents in cancer. After cellular uptake, the first limiting step is the ATP-dependent phosphorylation of nucleosides to form monophosphorylated nucleotides. These monophosphorylated nucleotides are incorporated into DNA in the place of cytosine. Then, DNMTs recognize the azacytosine-guanine dinucleotide and catalyze the methylation reaction by forming a covalent bond with the cytosine ring. The covalent complex at C6 cannot be resolved through b-elimination, because of the presence of a nitrogen atom at position 5. Covalently trapped DNMTs are degraded, resulting in the depletion of cellular DNMTs (PMID: 34452630). The two DNMT inhibitors azacitidine (5-Aza) and decitabine are hypomethylating agents (HMAs) currently approved for clinical use (PMID: 29301553). 6658	CCDC22-COMMD8-CUL1 complex		Human	HEK 293 cells	23563313	It is demonstrated that all COMMD proteins bind to CCDC22. Both memantine and ketamine inhibit NMDARs by occupying the NMDAR's ion channel and occluding current flow. Both drugs exhibit voltage dependence, entering the channel more quickly, leaving the channel more slowly, and inhibiting more effectively as a cell's membrane potential is hyperpolarized (PMID: 25462293). 7459	Glycine receptor (GLRA11, GLRB)		Human		22973015	The glycine receptor chloride channel (GlyR), a member of the pentameric Cys-loop ion channel receptor family, mediates inhibitory neurotransmission in the spinal cord, brainstem and retina. 7490	KDR-VEGF165 complex	VEGF-A165-VEGFR2 complex	Human	HUVECs	27044325	VEGF-A binding to VEGFR2 triggers distinct patterns of ubiquitylation, proteolysis and clearance within the endosome-lysosome system. VEGF-A isoforms had distinct properties in regulating VEGFR2 endocytosis at the plasma membrane, it was predicted that VEGF-A-stimulated VEGFR2 degradation was isoform-specific. It was confirmed that this was indeed true: VEGF-A121 showed negligible effects on VEGFR2 degradation; however, VEGF-A165 or VEGF-A145 showed a similar 30% reduction in total VEGFR2 levels after 120 min (PMID:7044325).	VEGF-A165 is a splice variant of VEGFA.		"The receptor tyrosine kinase inhibitors sorafenib, pazopanib or vandetanib all caused a concentration-dependent increase in the binding of the ligand VEGF165 to the receptor VEGFR2 (KDR) thereby preventing the internalization of VEGFR2 (KDR) into intracellular endosomes (PMID: 28392095).
The tyrosine kinase inhibitor axitinib is a selective inhibitor of VEGFR-1 (FLT1), -2 (KDR) and -3 (FLT4). Binding of axitinib to the kinase domain of VEGF receptors stabilizes an inactive conformation of the kinase, thus inhibiting signal transduction by VEGF (PMID: 19876699).
Cabozantinib malate effectively blocks binding of VEGFA121 and VEGFA165 to VEGFR2 (KDR) thereby inhibiting angiogenesis (PMID: 28296822).
The VEGFR2 tyrosine kinase inhibitor lenvatinib (E7080) is a potent inhibitor of angiogenesis via inhibition of VEGF/KDR and SCF/KIT signaling (PMID: 17943726; 25197551).
Nintedanib (BIBF 1120) is a VEGFR2 (KDR)-kinase inhibitor. By binding to the ATP-binding site of VEGFR2 (KDR) VEGFR activation is blocked. Treatment of VEGF-stimulated endothelial cells with BIBF 1120 resulted in inhibition of cell proliferation and apoptosis and affects tumor vessel density and pericytes (PMID: 18559524; 25474320). 
Ramucirumab (IMC-1121B) is a fully humanized IgG1 monoclonal antibody, targeting the extracellular domain of VEGF receptor 2 (VEGFR2). (PMID: 23803182). By binding to VEGFR2 ramucirumab blocks the interaction with the VEGFR2 ligands, including VEGF-A, VEGF-C, and VEGF-D (PMID: 38239196), resulting in potent inhibition of VEGF signaling pathway (PMID: 16682007).
Regorafenib (BAY 73-4506) inhibits VEGFR2 and VEGFR3 autophosphorylation in serum-deprived HuVECs and HuLECs following stimulation with VEGF-A or VEGF-C (PMID: 27734608; 24347491).
Ranibizumab binds to all isoforms of VEGFA and inhibits the binding of VEGFR2 (KDR) to the ligand (PMID: 27234973).
Aflibercept forms a homogenous 1:1 complex with multiple VEGFR1 and VEGFR2 ligands, including VEGF-A, VEGF-B, and PlGF thereby blocking not only the amino acids necessary for VEGFR1/R2 binding but also occludes the heparin-binding site on VEGF165 (PMID: 38239196; 27234973). 
The monoclonal antibody bevacizumab binds to all isoforms of VEGFA and prevents the interaction with VEGFR-1 and VEGFR-2 to inhibit the activation of VEGFR signaling pathways that promote angiogenesis (PMID: 38239196; 27234973; 24445500).
Brolucizumab binds to all isoforms of VEGF-A and blocks binding to VEGFR2. (PMID: 38239196; 31537892; 33197916).
Faricimab is a bispecific heterodimeric antibody which binds simultanously to VEGF and to angiopoietin-2 (Ang-2) and prevents the interaction of VEGF with VEGFR2 as well as the interaction of Ang-2 with TIE2. Faricimab is designed for the treatment of ocular diseases (PMID: 38239196). 
Pegaptanib is a 28-base RNA aptamer, which selectively binds to VEGF-A165 and prevents its binding to both VEGFR-1 (FLT1) and VEGFR-2 (KDR) (PMID: 38239196; 31537892; 9685413).
Endostatin, the 20-kDa proteolytic fragment of collagen XVIII, is a potent inhibitor of angiogenesis and recombinant endostatin was shown to inhibit tumor growth and metastasis. Endostatin interacts with KDR and blocks the binding of VEGFA (VEGF165) to KDR, thus inhibiting VEGF-induced signaling (PMID: 12029087).

Pazopanib (GW786034), is a multitargeted tyrosine kinase inhibitor targeting VEGFR-1, -2, and -3, PDGFR-A, -B, and c-Kit. Pazopanib binds to the ATP pocket of the tyrosine kinase on the internal domain of the receptor, inhibiting activation and downstream VEGFR signaling (PMID: 23359171).
Sunitinib (SU11248) is a multitargeted tyrosine kinase inhibitor of VEGFR-1, -2, -3, PDGFRs, KIT, FLT3, RET and CSF-1R. Sunitinib binds to the ATP pocket of the tyrosine kinase on the internal domain of the receptor, inhibiting activation and downstream VEGFR signaling (PMID: 23359171).
Nintedanib (BIBF 1120) is a multitargeted tyrosine kinase inhibitor which simultaneously acts on three key receptor families involved in angiogenesis: VEGFR1-3, PDGFRA,-B and FGFR1-4. Nintedanib binds to the ATP pocket of the tyrosine kinase on the internal domain of the receptor, inhibiting activation and downstream VEGFR signaling (PMID: 18559524, 23359171)." Brolucizumab binds to all isoforms of VEGF-A and blocks binding to VEGFR2. (PMID: 38239196; 31537892; 33197916).

7574	APP-PSEN1 complex	APP-PS1 complex	Human	human 293 and HS683 cells; transfected CHO cells	9223340	Mutations in the presenilin 1 (PS1) and presenilin 2 (PS2) genes increase the production of the highly amyloidogenic 42-residue form of amyloid beta-protein (Abeta42) in a variety of cell lines and transgenic mice. (PMID: 21045206)	The two DNMT inhibitors azacitidine (5-Aza) and decitabine are hypomethylating agents (HMAs) currently approved for clinical use (PMID: 29301553). They are the most commonly used nucleoside agents in cancer. After cellular uptake, the first limiting step is the ATP-dependent phosphorylation of nucleosides to form monophosphorylated nucleotides. These monophosphorylated nucleotides are incorporated into DNA in the place of cytosine. Then, DNMTs recognize the azacytosine-guanine dinucleotide and catalyze the methylation reaction by forming a covalent bond with the cytosine ring. 8303	GRIN1-GRIN2B-PRR7 complex		Human	HEK293 cells	27458189	The synaptic component Proline rich 7 (PRR7) accumulates in the nucleus of hippocampal neurons following NMDAR activity. Elevated c-Jun levels result in apoptosis and are evident in neurodegenerative disorders such as Alzheimer's disease and dementia and after global cerebral insults including stroke and epilepsy. Both memantine and ketamine inhibit NMDARs by occupying the NMDAR's ion channel and occluding current flow. Both drugs are open channel blockers: when the channel is closed, the drugs have little or no ability to enter an unblocked channel or to unbind after blocking the channel. Both drugs exhibit voltage dependence, entering the channel more quickly, leaving the channel more slowly, and inhibiting more effectively as a cell's membrane potential is hyperpolarized (PMID: 25462293). UHRF1 predicts predicts outcome in hepatoblastoma (HB) (PMID: 29507645).	The two DNMT inhibitors azacitidine (5-Aza) and decitabine are hypomethylating agents (HMAs) currently approved for clinical use (PMID: 29301553). They are the most commonly used nucleoside agents in cancer. After cellular uptake, the first limiting step is the ATP-dependent phosphorylation of nucleosides to form monophosphorylated nucleotides. These monophosphorylated nucleotides are incorporated into DNA in the place of cytosine. Then, DNMTs recognize the azacytosine-guanine dinucleotide and catalyze the methylation reaction by forming a covalent bond with the cytosine ring. The covalent complex at C6 cannot be resolved through b-elimination, because of the presence of a nitrogen atom at position 5. Covalently trapped DNMTs are degraded, resulting in the depletion of cellular DNMTs (PMID: 34452630). Zebularine is a DNMT1-specific mechanistic inhibitor (PMID: 17085482). 8684	HCN1-HCN3 complex		Human	HEK293 cells	12928435	Hyperpolarization-activated cyclic nucleotide-gated (HCN) channels underlie the control of rhythmic activity in cardiac and neuronal pacemaker cells. In HCN, the polarity of voltage dependence is uniquely reversed. Intracellular cyclic adenosine monophosphate (cAMP) levels tune the voltage response, enabling sympathetic nerve stimulation to increase the heart rate. HCN channels contain a K+ channel selectivity filter-forming sequence from which the amino acids create a unique structure that explains Na+ and K+ permeability (PMID: 12928435).	"HCN channel subunits assemble to a variety of different heteromers. Only one pair of channel subunits, HCN2 and HCN3, makes an exception and does not form a functional heteromer. Although HCN2 and HCN3 subunits could be easily detected in the plasma membrane, there was no obvious colocalization of the two proteins. In accordance with this finding HCN2 and HCN3 are not coimmunoprecipitated by specific antibodies. Interestingly, cells coexpressing HCN2 and HCN3 exhibited a significantly reduced current density compared with cells expressing HCN2 alone. One explanation for this result is that in the presence of HCN3 less functional HCN2 channel protein is inserted into the plasma membrane. Homomeric HCN3 channels can probably not compensate for the resulting reduction in current amplitude because for unknown reasons HCN3 produces notoriously small currents.

8685	HCN1-HCN4 complex		Human	HEK293 cells	12928435	Hyperpolarization-activated cyclic nucleotide-gated (HCN) channels underlie the control of rhythmic activity in cardiac and neuronal pacemaker cells. In HCN, the polarity of voltage dependence is uniquely reversed. Intracellular cyclic adenosine monophosphate (cAMP) levels tune the voltage response, enabling sympathetic nerve stimulation to increase the heart rate. HCN channels contain a K+ channel selectivity filter-forming sequence from which the amino acids create a unique structure that explains Na+ and K+ permeability (PMID: 28086084).	CN channel subunits assemble to a variety of different heteromers. Only one pair of channel subunits, HCN2 and HCN3, makes an exception and does not form a functional heteromer. Although HCN2 and HCN3 subunits could be easily detected in the plasma membrane, there was no obvious colocalization of the two proteins. In accordance with this finding HCN2 and HCN3 are not coimmunoprecipitated by specific antibodies. Interestingly, cells coexpressing HCN2 and HCN3 exhibited a significantly reduced current density compared with cells expressing HCN2 alone. One explanation for this result is that in the presence of HCN3 less functional HCN2 channel protein is inserted into the plasma membrane. Homomeric HCN3 channels can probably not compensate for the resulting reduction in current amplitude because for unknown reasons HCN3 produces notoriously small currents. AChE associated with beta-amyloid deposits present in Alzheimer’s brain may be a relevant factor in triggering the neurodegeneration induced by senile plaques in specific regions of the brain (PMID: 9547230).	"Cholinesterase inhibitors enhance cholinergic transmission directly by inhibiting the enzyme acetylcholinesterase (AChE) which hydrolyses acetylcholine. AChE inhibition has been documented as a critical target for the effective management of Alzheimer Disease (AD) by an increase in the availability of acetylcholine in the brain regions and decrease in the Abeta deposition. Dual binding site inhibitors bind to both active and peripheral sites of AChE and thus, inhibit amyloid formation which is beneficial for the treatment in AD. Tacrine, donepezil, rivastigmine and galantamine are clinically employed AChE inhibitors for the management of AD (PMID: 23435942). Tacrine was withdrawn from the market in 2013 due to its hepatotoxicity (PMID: 31311169). Aducanumab reduced brain amyloid-beta plaques in a time- and dose-dependent manner and a slowed decline in cognition in the high-dose treated group. It has been the first drug targeting the AD pathologic hallmark and has effectively reduced the clinical progression of the disease, however, was only effective in the mild or early stages of AD (PMID: 36775284).
Lecanemab (Leqembi) did not slow cognitive decline in APOE4 carriers; rather, it enhanced the decline in study participants with 2 APOE4 genes (PMID: 37676096)."	"[ACHE; Abeta-ACHE complex; 8857; tacrine; inhibits; complex formation; 23435942]

8862	COX2 complex	PTGS2 complex	Human	in vitro	26859324	Cyclooxygenase enzymes (COX-1 and COX-2) are bifunctional homodimeric enzymes that oxygenate arachidonic acid to generate prostaglandin H2 in the committed step of prostaglandin biosynthesis. Prostaglandin H2 serves as the major substrate for downstream synthases that give rise to this potent class of signaling molecules, which are responsible for the control of physiological housekeeping functions, including the regulation of renal water and sodium metabolism, parturition, and stomach acid secretion.		Abnormal changes in prostaglandin production are associated with various disease pathologies, including inflammation, cardiovascular disease, and cancer.	In a human whole blood assay, it was shown that the nonsteroid anti- inflammatory drugs aspirin, diclofenac, diflunisal, fenoprofen, flufenamic acid, flurbiprofen, ibuprofen, indomethacin, ketoprofen, ketorolac, meclofenamic acid, mefenamic acid, naproxen, aminosalicylic acid (=mesalazine), piroxicam, sulfasalazine and tolmetin inhibit the activity of the PTGS2 (COX-2) complex (PMID: 10377455). In a study it was shown, that in leucocytes acemetacin inhibits the activity of the PTGS2 complex more potently than in gastric mucosa (PMID: 8144313). In an animal model, it was shown that bromfenac was approximately 32 times more active against PTGS2 complex than PTGS1 complex (PMID: 16846546). In rat adjuvant-induced arthritis (AIA) model, it was shown that felbinac and loxofrofen inhibit the activity of the PTGS1 complex and the PTGS2 complex (PMID: 27241582). In a study with Thai healthy volunteers, it was shown that floctafenine inhibits the activity of the PTGS1 complex and the PTGS2 complex (PMID: 23755755). In the eye, nepafenac is converted to an active metabolite, amfenac, which like nepafenac is a reversible inhibitor of the PTGS1 complex and the PTGS2 complex (PMID: 19897019). In vitro studies on the two isoforms of COX enzyme, performed on human platelets and human synovial fluid cells, demonstrated that oxaprozin inhibits the PTGS1 complex and the PTGS2 complex (PMID: 15324530). Piketoprofen has been described as inhibitor of the PTGS2 complex (PMID: 34592918). After demonstrating that tiaprofenic acid (RMD86) presents in vivo antinociceptive and antipyretic effects, a molecular docking was shown for two enzymes greatly involved in inflammatory processes, the PTGS1 complex and the PTGS2 complex (PMID: 33294672). In a whole blood assay from healthy volunteers, it was shown that bismuth subsalicylate inhibits the activity of the PTGS1 complex and the PTGS2 complex (PMID: 9626023). Mesalazine, also known as 5-aminosalicylic acid (5-ASA) can also inhibit COX-2 at the level of RNA and protein, which is associated with a significant reduction in prostaglandin E2 (PGE2) synthesis (PMID: 34410540). Balsalazide, a pro-drug of 5-ASA, significantly suppressed COX-2 expression and induced 15-PGDH expression in HT-29 cells (PMID: 22493349). Aceclofenac is superior from other NSAIDs as it has selectivity for Cox-2, a beneficial Cox inhibitor, well-tolerated, and improved cardiovascular safety than other selective Cox-2 inhibitors (PMID: 22171305). In vitro studies have shown that celecoxib and rofecoxib are selective inhibitors of the COX2 complex (PMID: 11520213). Etodolac In CHO cells stably transfected with human COX2, etodolac was shown to be an efficient inhibitor of COX2 (PMID: 9146894). In microsomal assays using human COX-1 and COX-2, Meloxicam inhibited COX-2 more selectivity than piroxicam and other marketed NSAIDs (PMID: 9083488). Imrecoxib was shown to selectively and dose-dependently inhibit COX-2 mRNA level (PMID: 15210067). Using standard assays, lumiracoxib was found to be a poor inhibitor of purified ovine COX-1 and a relatively weak inhibitor of purified human COX-2 (PMID: 17434872). Nabumetone is a relatively selective COX-2 inhibitor (PMID: 9435990). Oral administration of 1000 mg paracetamol to human volunteers inhibits blood monocyte cyclooxygenase (COX)-2 by more than 80%, i.e., to a comparable degree as NSAIDs and selective COX-2 inhibitors (PMID: 17884974). Parecoxib is a water-soluble prodrug of valdecoxib, a non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drug (NSAID). Valdecoxib potently inhibits recombinant human COX-2 (PMID: 15494548). Polmacoxib (CG100649) is a novel NSAID proposed to inhibit both COX-2 and carbonic anhydrase (CA)-I/-II (PMID: 22278334). In CHO cells, stably expressed sulindac is a potent inhibitor of both human COX-1 and COX-2 (PMID: 8945508). We have not found any information about the effect of alclofenac or olsalazine on the COX2 complex.	"[PTGS2; COX2 complex; 8862; acetylsalicylic acid; inhibits; complex activity; 10377455]

LXR can also be activated by heterodimerization alone in the absence of a ligand, via a mechanism referred to as ‘‘dimerization-induced activation” (PMID: 9199332). 8936	NMDA receptor complex (GRIN1, GRIN2B)	NR1-NR2B complex	Human	HEK293 cells	19793963	NMDA receptors comprised of different NR2 subunits exhibit strikingly unique biophysical and pharmacological properties. The extracellular amino-terminal domain (ATD) of the NR2 subunit controls pharmacological and kinetic properties of recombinant NMDA receptors, such as agonist potency, deactivation time course, open probability (P(OPEN)), and mean open/shut duration (PMID: 19793963).		NMDA receptors play key roles in physiological processes, such as neuronal development, synaptic plasticity, and learning, as well as in a number of pathophysiological conditions including epilepsy, ischemic damage, neurodegenerative diseases, and psychiatric disorders (PMID: 19793963).	Both memantine and ketamine inhibit NMDARs by occupying the NMDAR's ion channel and occluding current flow. Both drugs are open channel blockers: when the channel is closed, the drugs have little or no ability to enter an unblocked channel or to unbind after blocking the channel. Both drugs exhibit voltage dependence, entering the channel more quickly, leaving the channel more slowly, and inhibiting more effectively as a cell's membrane potential is hyperpolarized (PMID: 25462293). Acamprosate displayes only a weak antagonist activity against NMDA-induced currents in HEK-293 cells expressing NR1-1a/NR2A or NR1-1a/NR2B receptors (PMID: 11369029) and produces its anti-relapse effects via calcium (PMID: 24081303). The anticonvulsant felbamate blocks N-methyl-D-asparate (NMDA) receptors with NR1A subunit, and either the NR2A, NR2B or NR2C subunits (PMID: 10690753). Amantadine inhibits the NMDA receptors NR1/NR2B by accelerating channel closure during channel block (PMID: 15800186). The GluN1a-2D NMDAR tetramer has a pseudo-symmetrical subunit arrangement where two GluN2D subunits within the tetramer have similar ATD-LBD (amino-terminal domain / ligand-binding domain) orientations like GluN1a-2A, GluN1-2B, or GluN1-2A-2B NMDARs but unlike the GluN1a-2C or GluN1a-2A-2C NMDARs (PMID: 36309015).	NMDARs are obligate heterotetramers composed of GluN1 subunits in combination with GluN2 and/or GluN3 subunits (PMID: 25462293).	NMDA receptors has been implicated in many diseases and injuries including stroke, Parkinson’s disease, Huntington’s disease and schizophrenia (PMID: 16281028).	Both memantine and ketamine inhibit NMDARs by occupying the NMDAR's ion channel and occluding current flow. Both drugs are open channel blockers: when the channel is closed, the drugs have little or no ability to enter an unblocked channel or to unbind after blocking the channel. Both drugs exhibit voltage dependence, entering the channel more quickly, leaving the channel more slowly, and inhibiting more effectively as a cell's membrane potential is hyperpolarized (PMID: 25462293). Acamprosate displayes only a weak antagonist activity against NMDA-induced currents in HEK-293 cells expressing NR1-1a/NR2A or NR1-1a/NR2B receptors (PMID: 11369029) and produces its anti-relapse effects via calcium (PMID: 24081303). The anticonvulsant felbamate blocks N-methyl-D-asparate (NMDA) receptors with NR1A subunit, and either the NR2A, NR2B or NR2C subunits (PMID: 10690753). 9034	AGTR1-BDKRB2 complex		Human	HEK-293 cells	10993080	The vasopressor angiotensin II regulates vascular contractility and blood pressure through binding to type 1 angiotensin II receptors (AT1). Bradykinin, a vasodepressor, is a functional antagonist of angiotensin II. The two hormone systems are interconnected by the angiotensin-converting enzyme, which releases angiotensin II from its precursor and inactivates the vasodepressor bradykinin. The AT1 receptor and the bradykinin (B2) receptor also communicate directly with each other. They form stable heterodimers, causing increased activation of G alpha(q) and G alpha(i) proteins, the two major signalling proteins triggered by AT1. Furthermore, the endocytotic pathway of both receptors changed with heterodimerization (PMID: 10993080).		"Increased complex formation between angiotensin II AT1 and bradykinin B2, two G protein-coupled receptors with opposing effects on blood vessel constriction, triggers symptoms of preeclampsia in pregnant mice. Aberrant heteromerization of AT1-B2 led to exaggerated calcium signaling and high vascular smooth muscle mechanosensitivity, which could explain the onset of preeclampsia symptoms at late-stage pregnancy as mechanical forces increase with fetal mass. AT1-B2 heteromerization was found to occur in human placental biopsies from pregnancies complicated by preeclampsia (PMID: 30503206).
In preeclamptic hypertensive women, a significant increase in heterodimerization occurs between the AT1-receptor for the vasopressor angiotensin II and the B2-receptor for the vasodepressor bradykinin. The results suggest that AT1-B2 heterodimers contribute to angiotensin II hypersensitivity in preeclampsia ( PMID: 11533702)." 9088	AGAP1-GUCY1A1-GUCY1B1 complex	GGAP1-GUCY1A3-GUCY1B3 complex	Human	human tissue, HEK293 cells, HeLa cells	15381706	AGAP1 associates with both the alpha1 and beta1 subunits of sGC. This complex formation between these proteins is modulated by tyrosine phosphorylation. It is proposed that AGAP1, by binding to sGC, may help regulate the intracellular distribution of sGC and thus the local delivery of cGMP in mammalian cells (PMID: 15381706).			Soluble guanylate cyclase (sGC), catalyzing the conversion of GTP to cGMP, is the primary receptor for and activated by the ligand nitric oxide (NO) in mammalians (PMID: 31514202; 31566566). NO (nitric oxide) binds to sGC, which is a heterodimeric enzyme consisting of an alpha and beta subunit carrying an N-heme-NO binding domain. The major isoforms are sGCalpha1beta1 and sGCalpha2beta1 encoded by GUCY1A1, GUCY1B1, and GUCY1A2, respectively. NO-dependent sGC stimulation triggers formation of cGMP, which is the cellular second messenger. sGC is therefore a key signal transducer of NO-mediated organ effects (PMID: 37023747). 9232	PDE5A homodimer		Human	in vitro	15677448	The cGMP-binding cGMP-specific phosphodiesterase (PDE5) contains a catalytic domain that hydrolyzes cGMP and a regulatory (R) domain. The R domain binds cGMP allosterically, provides for dimerization, and is phosphorylated at a site regulated by allosteric cGMP binding (PMID: 15677448). PDE5 mediates the hydrolysis of the cyclic nucleotide cGMP into its inactive form. Levels of PDE5 in the temporal cortex of AD patients are significantly higher than those of age-matched healthy control subjects. Inhibition of PDE5 suppresses cGMP hydrolysis, resulting in the activation of protein kinase G (PKG) and increased phosphorylation of CREB at Ser133, which rescues LTP impairment and cognitive dysfunction in an amyloid precursor protein/presenilin-1 (APP/PS1) AD mouse mode (PMID: 35804462).	human cDNA expressed in Sf9 cells;	PDE5 is the target of sildenafil (Viagra TM), tadalafil (Cialis TM), and vardenafil (LevitraTM), all of which are in use for treatment of maladies associated with vascular disease (PMID: 15677448).	In PDE5 holoenzyme, allosteric cGMP binding increases the catalytic site binding affinity for the inhibitors sildenafil, tadalafil, and vardenafil (PMID: 15677448). The PDE5 inhibitor sildenafil improves memory function and reverses cognitive deficits by restoring CREB signaling in APP/PS1 and aged Tg2576 transgenic AD. The oral administration of sildenafil increases CBF and cerebral oxygen metabolism in AD patients. The PDE5 inhibitor, tadalafil, enhances spatial memory by decreasing tau protein levels in J20 transgenic AD mice. (PMID: 35804462). The PDE5 inhibitor udenafil improves insulin sensitivity by increasing mitochondrial function in adipocytes and ameliorates nonalcoholic fatty liver disease by improving mitochondrial function (PMID: 33895552). The blood-brain barrier penetrating phosphodiesterase 5 (PDE5) inhibitor, mirodenafil (5-ethyl-2-7-n-propyl-3,5-dihydrro-4H-pyrrolo[3,2-d]pyrimidin-4-one), ameliorates Alzheimer-like pathology and symptoms (PMID: 35804462). Dipyridamole is a potential pharmacological agent to prevent vascular stenosis because of its antiproliferative properties. Dipyridamole caused an enrichment of cells in G(0)/G(1) and a corresponding reduction of cells in S phase. It primarily targets PDE5, the major cGMP hydrolyzing enzyme in vascular smooth muscle (PMID: 17169124). Neuroprotective efficacy of dipyridamole in human patients appears unlikely, since it does not penetrate the blood-brain barrier. It has little effects on cAMP but mainly elevates cGMP levels (PMID: 28904388). Pentoxifylline (PTX) is  nonspecific PDE inhibitor, e.g. known to stimulate sperm motility in vitro and has been used to treat sperm prior to insemination (PMID: 29256125). 9451	PIK3CD-PIK3R1 complex	p110delta-p85alpha complex	Human	human leukocytes	9235916	PI3Ks generate lipid second messengers that serve as membrane docking sites for a variety of downstream effector proteins such as protein kinases, regulators of small GTPases, and scaffolding proteins (PMID: 9235916).	Class IA phosphoinositide 3-kinases (PI3Ks) are obligate catalytic p110 and regulatory p85 heterodimers. These heterodimers consist of a p110 catalytic subunit (p110alpha/PIK3CA, p110beta/PIK3CB, or p110delta/PIK3CD) bound to any of the distinct regulatory subunits (p85alpha/PIK3R1, p85beta/PIK3R2, or p55/PIK3R3) (PMID: 17470792). 		"Duvelisib inhibits the isoform delta of PI3K which is necessary for cell proliferation and survival and the isoform gamma which is critical for cytokine signaling and the pro-inflammatory response. Owing to its anti-inflammatory responses, duvelisib has promise for inflammatory diseases such as asthma, rheumatoid arthritis, and lupus nephritis (PMID: 28388280). Copanlisib inhibits the catalytic activity of all four PI3Kisoforms (P110alpha, P110beta, P110delta, and P110gamma), with the highest selectivity for the PI3Kalpha and PI3Kdelta isoforms. These isoforms are commonly found in malignant B cells, namely chronic lymphocytic lymphoma (CLL) and diffuse large B cell lymphoma (DLBCL) (PMID: 33889376). Idelalisib is an orally available, small molecule inhibitor of phosphatidylinositol 3-kinase delta (PI3Kdelta), which is an essential component in the B cell signaling pathways that drive migration of B cells to lymph nodes and bone marrow. Inhibition of this pathway inhibits B cell chemotaxis and adherence and reduces cell viability. It is approved for use in combination with rituximab in relapsed or refractory chronic lymphocytic leukemia (CLL) and as monotherapy for relapsed follicular B cell, small lymphocytic lymphoma and indolent non-Hodgkin lymphoma (PMID: 31644147). Umbralisib is an oral, first-in-class dual phosphatidylinositol 3-kinase delta (PI3Kdelta) and casein kinase 1 epsilon (CK1epsilon) inhibitor being developed for the treatment of various haematological malignancies. Umbralisib enhanced the anti-tumour activity of brentuximab, resulting in marked anti-mitotic and cytotoxic effects in Hodgkin-derived cell lines and synergized with carfilzomib to inhibit cap-dependent translation of tumour promoting genes in diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (DLBCL) and mantle cell lymphoma (MCL) cell lines (PMID: 33797740). Leniolisib is structurally unique relative to other approved PI3Kd inhibitors; it is not propeller-shaped. Instead of binding to the specificity pocket, leniolisib uses a tryptophan shelf and stacks with Trp760 in p110delta, whereas the corresponding interaction with Trp780 in p110alpha is prevented, thus conferring specificity for the delta isoform (PMID: 37777067).

9641	HDAC4-MEF2A complex		Human	HEK293T cells	10737771	Myocyte enhancer factor (MEF)-2 plays a critical role in proliferation, differentiation, and development of various cell types in a tissue specific manner. Four isoforms of MEF-2 (A-D) differentially participate in controlling the cell fate during the developmental phases of cardiac, muscle, vascular, immune and skeletal systems. MEF2 interacts with histone deacetylases (HDACs) 4 and 5, resulting in repression of the transcriptional activity of MEF2 (PMID: 10737771). HDAC4, unlike other deacetylases, shuttles between the nucleus and the cytoplasm in a process involving active nuclear export. In the nucleus, HDAC4 associates with the myocyte enhancer factor MEF2A. Binding of HDAC4 to MEF2A results in the repression of MEF2A transcriptional activation, a function that requires the deacetylase domain of HDAC4 (PMID: 10487761).		The HDAC-MEF-2 axis has been implicated in various cancers. Increased expression of class IIa HDACs has been correlated with suppression of MEF-2 transcriptional activity and poor prognosis of estrogen receptor-positive (ER+) breast tumors as well as increased proliferation of mammary epithelial cells (PMID: 10737771). Panobinostat is a hydroxamic acid derivative and also a pan-HDAC inhibitor. Romidepsin, a depsipeptide, is a selective inhibitor of class I HDACs, specifically HDAC1 and 2 (PMID: 31105874). 9788	CASR-GNAQ-GNB1-GNG2 complex		Human	in vitro	37919470	The human calcium-sensing receptor (CaSR) is a class C G protein-coupled receptor (GPCR) responsible for maintaining Ca2+ homeostasis in blood. 9801	Extracellular calcium-sensing receptor	CASR homodimer	Human	HEK293 cells	9722601	"The extracellular calcium-sensing receptor (CaSR) is a G protein-coupled receptor that plays important roles in calcium homeostasis.The CaSR resides on the cell surface as homodimers that likely represent the active form of the receptor (PMID: 9722601).
The calcium-sensing receptor (CaSR) is a class C G protein-coupled receptor that responds to multiple endogenous agonists and allosteric modulators, including divalent and trivalent cations, L-amino acids, gamma-glutamyl peptides, polyamines, polycationic peptides, and protons (PMID: 32467152)."		"Mutations in the calcium-sensing receptor (CaSR) cause calcium-handling diseases. Familial hypocalciuric hypercalcemia is associated to GPCR misfolding and loss-of-function of the abnormal receptor. Allosteric agonists, such as NPS R-568, have been shown to stabilize CaSR mutants. NPS
R-568 is a cotranslational stabilizer acting at a conformational checkpoint during CaSR biosynthesis. A number of CaSR Class II loss-of-function mutants leading to familial hypocalciuric hypercalcemia and neonatal hyperparathyrodism can be stabilized and rescued by NPS R-568 (PMID: 34830210)."	"Cinacalcet, a positive allosteric modulator of the calcium sensing receptor (CaSR) reduces parathyroid hormone (PTH) secretion by increasing the sensitivity of the CaSR on parathyroid cells (PMID: 35041148).
The CaSR plays a critical role in extracellular calcium homeostasis, as demonstrated by the many naturally occurring mutations in the CaSR or its signaling partners that cause calcium homeostasis disorders. However, CaSR tissue expression in mammals is broad and includes tissues unrelated to calcium homeostasis, in which it, for example, regulates the secretion of digestive hormones, airway constriction, cardiovascular effects, cellular differentiation, and proliferation. Thus, although the CaSR is targeted clinically by the positive allosteric modulators (PAMs) cinacalcet, evocalcet, and etelcalcetide in hyperparathyroidism, it is also a putative therapeutic target in diabetes, asthma, cardiovascular disease, and cancer (PMID: 32467152).
Upacicalcet, a positive allosteric modulator of the calcium-sensing receptor, prevents vascular calcification and bone disorder in a rat adenine-induced secondary hyperparathyroidism model (PMID: 36395959)." 9850	GHRHR-PICK1 complex		Human	HEK293 cells	23823934	Release of growth hormone (GH) from the somatotroph is regulated by binding GH-releasing hormone (GHRH) to its cognate receptor (GHRHR), one of the members of the G protein-coupled receptor (GPCR) superfamily. 9888	Growth hormone receptor	GHR homodimer	Human	in vitro	34193419	The human growth hormone receptor (hGHR) is ubiquitously expressed and is activated by human growth hormone (hGH), produced in the pituitary gland. hGHR is important for regulating growth at a cellular and systemic level and is involved in the regulation of hepatic metabolism, cardiac function, bone turnover, and the immune system. Besides direct promotion of growth, its ligand hGH can also indirectly regulate growth by initiating the synthesis of insulin-like growth factor-I, an important factor in postnatal growth. The results of this study suggested that the hGHR-GFP can form dimers in the absence of hGH, most likely through the transmembrane region (PMID: 34193419).	The growth hormone receptor GHR is post-translationally cleaved to produce soluble growth hormone-binding protein GHBP. The protein in this complex is GHR.	Excess hGH production and mutations in the hGHR gene manifest in different diseases including cancer and growth deficiencies, with associated cardiovascular, metabolic, and respiratory difficulties (PMID: 34193419).	"Pegvisomant is a growth hormone receptor antagonist (PMID: 12372843).
Growth hormone (GH) is indicated for therapy of growth hormone deficiency (GHD) in pediatric and adult patients. Introduction of recombinant human GH (rhGH) improved access to GH therapy. Norditropin [ somatropin (rDNA origin) injection] is rhGH, used for the replacement of endogenous GH in children and adults with GHD (PMID: 23662811).
In a multicentre clinical trial 54 children aged 4.0 to 17.3 years, who had growth hormone deficiency that had not previously been treated, were given biosynthetic methionyl growth hormone (somatrem) 4 units three times a week by subcutaneous or intramuscular injection for one year. 9983	CBFA2T3-PDE4A-PRKAR2A complex	MTG16B-PDE4A-PKA complex	Human	Jurkat cells, HuT 78 cells	15470020	The cAMP protein kinase A (PKA) pathway in T cells conveys an inhibitory signal to suppress inflammation. A-kinase anchoring proteins (AKAPs) bind and target PKA to various subcellular locations. AKAPs also bind other signaling molecules such as cyclic nucleotide phosphodiesterases (PDEs) that hydrolyze cAMP in the cell. PDEs are involved in all aspects of cellular regulation, e.g. PDE4 and PDE7 have important roles in T cell activation. "Pralmorelin (GHRP 2, growth hormone-releasing peptide 2) is an orally active, synthetic growth hormone-releasing peptide. Cancer anorexia-cachexia syndrome is a multifactorial condition characterized by significant weight loss due to muscle loss. It is associated with functional impairment, changes in body composition and nutritional disorders. Ghrelin receptors are involved in the release of growth hormone (GH) in the pituitary gland and increase appetite via the hypothalamus. 10015	Oxytocin receptor	OXTR homodimer	Human	COS-7 cells	15089977	"Oxytocin/vasopressin receptors constitute a subgroup within the family of G-protein-coupled receptors, and include the oxytocin receptor, and the vasopressin receptor subtypes V1a, V1band V2. With the exception of the V2 receptor, which activates adenylyl cyclase in response to agonist binding, the remaining members of this group are able to activate phospholipase C. The oxytocin receptor can couple functionally to both Gq/11 and Gi proteins. Oxytocin-receptor activation triggers multiple molecular events, including an increase in intracellular free calcium concentration, activation of mitogen-activated protein (MAP) kinase, protein kinase C and myosin light-chain kinase, and synthesis of prostaglandin E2. Agonists (DOI and quinpirol) decreased the FRET value while antagonists (ketanserin and butaclamol) increased the FRET value (PMID: 20831885).
The serotonin 5-HT(2A) receptors form homo- and hetero-dimers with the dopamine D(2) receptors and polymorphism H452Y within the 5-HT(2A) receptor, implicated as a cause of altered response to antipsychotic treatment, disturbs both processes. Clozapine affected the hetero-dimers (5-HT(2A)H452Y/D(2)) complexes and increased the otherwise weakened dimerization to the value observed for combination of both wild type receptors, and had no effect on the serotonin receptor homo-dimers (5-HT(2A)H452Y/5-HT(2A)), while haloperidol has restored the weakened interaction within homo-complexes and did not effect the hetero-complexes. The obtained data suggest that H452Y polymorphism has an influence not only on the level of constitutive oligomerization of investigated receptors but also it changes their pharmacological properties within both homo- and hetero-complexes (PMID: 21496455)." 10108	ADORA2A-ADORA2B complex	Adenosine A2A/A2B receptor heterodimer	Human	CHO-K1 cells	29568380	The adenosine receptor (AR) subtypes A2A and A2B are rhodopsin-like Gs protein-coupled receptors whose expression is highly regulated under pathological, e.g. hypoxic, ischemic and inflammatory conditions. "TRPV1 and TRPA1 were activated by paracetamol in vivo (PMID: 32051870).
TRPV1 is a non-selective cation channel; when it is activated by capsaicin, sodium and calcium ions flowing through TRPV1 into the cell to depolarize nociceptive neurons, leading to action potential firing and finally the sensation of spiciness (PMID: 9349813).
Capsaicin binds to a pocket formed by the channel’s transmembrane segments, where it takes a “tail-up, head-down” configuration. Binding is mediated by both hydrogen bonds and van der Waals interactions. Upon binding, capsaicin stabilizes the open state of TRPV1 by “pull-and-contact” with the S4-S5 linker (PMID: 28044278)
At physiological concentrations, CBD (cannabidiol) inhibits TRPV1 signaling by a dual mechanism: the first by inhibiting the adenylyl 
cyclase – cAMP pathway, which is essential for maintaining TRPV1 sensitization. The second pathway likely involves calcineurin-mediated TRPV1 inhibition. Both mechanisms may underlie nociceptor desensitization and the therapeutic effect of CBD in animal models and patients with acute and chronic pain (PMID: 32982390).
 Assuming the CBD binding site in TRPV1 is the same as that of TRPV2, this orientation of tyrosine would likely have minimal impact in the binding affinity of CBD, especially due to the reported role of Y634 in TRPV2 as a hydrophobic shield from water in the pore. Due to this, it is possible that Y672 in TRPV1 is still providing some degree of hydrophobic shielding for CBD should it bind in the same location, while the lipophilic interactions via L577 and surrounding lipophilic residues remain intact (PMID: 33362478)." 10223	DNMT3A-EZH2 complex		Human	HEK293T cells, OCI-AML3 cells	34067359	DNMT3A is responsible for de novo DNA methylation. EZH2 interacts with the conserved PHD-like motifs in DNMT3A and DNMT3B, and direct physical contact between EZH2 and DNMT3A is necessary to control CpG methylation of promoters in the EZH2 target genes MYT1, WNT1, KCNA1, and CRN1. The two DNMT inhibitors azacitidine (5-Aza) and decitabine are hypomethylating agents (HMAs) currently approved for clinical use (PMID: 29301553). They are the most commonly used nucleoside agents in cancer. After cellular uptake, the first limiting step is the ATP-dependent phosphorylation of nucleosides to form monophosphorylated nucleotides. These monophosphorylated nucleotides are incorporated into DNA in the place of cytosine. Then, DNMTs recognize the azacytosine-guanine dinucleotide and catalyze the methylation reaction by forming a covalent bond with the cytosine ring. The covalent complex at C6 cannot be resolved through b-elimination, because of the presence of a nitrogen atom at position 5. Covalently trapped DNMTs are degraded, resulting in the depletion of cellular DNMTs. Decitabine can decrease DNMT1 and DNMT3A expression, reversing abnormal transcription activation, while azacitidine only targets DNMT1 (PMID: 34452630). 10308	ADRA1B-EEA1 complex, norepinephrine-stimulated	ADRA1B-EEA1 complex, noradrenalin-stimulated	Human	HEK293 cells	25799564	The Rab GTPase family controls endocytosis, vesicular trafficking, and endosomal fusion. Among their properties is the differential distribution of its members on the surface of various organelles. 10342	Alpha-2A adrenergic receptor	ADRA2A homodimer	Human	HEK293 cells	16605244	Three human alpha2-adrenergic receptor subtypes (alpha2-ARs) have been cloned and are denoted alpha2A, alpha2B, and alpha2C. All three subtypes couple to G-alpha-i and are activated by the endogenous agonists epinephrine and norepinephrine. The subtypes alpha2A and alpha2C are both expressed on presynaptic nerves and act to inhibit norepinephrine release via negative feedback (PMID: 16605244).			"Epinephrine and norepinephrine are non-selective adrenic receptor agonists, their actions result from the activation of nine different adrenoreceptors (PMID: 30740663).
Apraclonidine is an alpha2-adrenergic agonist, which causes Müller muscles to contract quickly elevating the upper eyelid 1-3 mm. Apraclonidine is used to treat glaucoma and Horner syndrome because of its effects to increase muscle tone and decrease intraocular pressure (PMID: 157485500).
Brimonidine is a selective alpha2-adrenergic receptor (AR) agonist approved for persistent facial erythema of rosacea (PMID: 27562835).
Clonidine is a presynaptic alpha2-adrenergic receptor agonist that has been used for many years to treat hypertension and other conditions, including chronic pain (PMID: 35587172).
Dexmedetomidine (DEX) is a highly selective alpha2-adrenoceptor agonist that is widely used in intensive and anesthetic care for its sedative and anxiolytic properties (PMID: 38481729).
Dipivefrin is an alpha/beta-adrenergic agonist (PMID: 8357055).
Droxidopa is an oral prodrug of norepinephrine (PMID: 25487613).
Guanfacine is an alpha2A-adrenergic receptor agonist (PMID: 26585576).
Lofexidine is an alpha2- adrenergic receptor agonist for opioid detoxification (PMID: 20040696).
With respect to centrally acting alpha 2-adrenoceptor agonists, clonidine, guanfacine and alpha-methyldopa are the prototypes (PMID: 2841084).
Phenoxybenzamine is a non-selective antagonist at both alpha 1- and alpha 2-adrenoceptors (PMID: 9122046).
Phentolamine is an FDA approved non-selective alpha-adrenergic blocker, clinically prescribed for oral anesthesia reversal, hypertension, and erectile dysfunction (PMID: 35228612).
The central alpha2 adrenoceptor agonist tizanidine is a myotonolytic agent used in the treatment of spasticity in patients with cerebral or spinal injury (PMID: 9074844).
Tolazoline, an alpha-adrenergic blocking agent useful in the treatment of persistent pulmonary hypertension of the neonate induces intense renal vasoconstriction with consequent hypoperfusion (PMID: 2901276).
Naphazoline, a nonspecific alpha-adrenoceptor stimulant, is a potent vasoconstrictor used in nasal sprays, eye drops, and over-the-counter antiseptics (PMID: 38155033).
Tetrahydrozoline is an imidazoline derivative with alpha receptor agonist activity (PMID: 18259967).
Guanabenz is a central alpha2 adrenoreceptor agonist (PMID: 6679138).

10343	Alpha-2C adrenergic receptor	ADRA2C homodimer	Human	HEK293 cells	16605244	Three human alpha2-adrenergic receptor subtypes (alpha2-ARs) have been cloned and are denoted alpha2A, alpha2B, and alpha2C. The subtypes alpha2A and alpha2C are both expressed on presynaptic nerves and act to inhibit norepinephrine release via negative feedback (PMID: 16605244).			"Epinephrine and norepinephrine are non-selective adrenic receptor agonists, their actions result from the activation of nine different adrenoreceptors (PMID: 30740663).
Apraclonidine is an alpha2-adrenergic agonist, which causes Müller muscles to contract quickly elevating the upper eyelid 1-3 mm. Apraclonidine is used to treat glaucoma and Horner syndrome because of its effects to increase muscle tone and decrease intraocular pressure (PMID: 157485500).
Brimonidine is a selective alpha2-adrenergic receptor (AR) agonist approved for persistent facial erythema of rosacea (PMID: 27562835).
Clonidine is a presynaptic alpha2-adrenergic receptor agonist that has been used for many years to treat hypertension and other conditions, including chronic pain (PMID: 35587172).
Dexmedetomidine (DEX) is a highly selective alpha2-adrenoceptor agonist that is widely used in intensive and anesthetic care for its sedative and anxiolytic properties (PMID: 38481729).
Dipivefrin is an alpha/beta-adrenergic agonist (PMID: 8357055).
Droxidopa is an oral prodrug of norepinephrine (PMID: 25487613).
Phentolamine is an FDA approved non-selective alpha-adrenergic blocker, clinically prescribed for oral anesthesia reversal, hypertension, and erectile dysfunction (PMID: 35228612).
The central alpha2 adrenoceptor agonist tizanidine is a myotonolytic agent used in the treatment of spasticity in patients with cerebral or spinal injury (PMID: 9074844).
Tolazoline, an alpha-adrenergic blocking agent useful in the treatment of persistent pulmonary hypertension of the neonate induces intense renal vasoconstriction with consequent hypoperfusion (PMID: 2901276).
Naphazoline, a nonspecific alpha-adrenoceptor stimulant, is a potent vasoconstrictor used in nasal sprays, eye drops, and over-the-counter antiseptics (PMID: 38155033).
Tetrahydrozoline is an imidazoline derivative with alpha receptor agonist activity (PMID: 18259967).
Guanabenz is a central alpha2 adrenoreceptor agonist (PMID: 6679138)."	"[ADRA2C; Alpha-2C adrenergic receptor; 10343; epinephrine; activates; complex activity; 30740663]
