"Nadolol, penbutolol, pindolol, propranolol, and timolol are non-selective first generation beta-blockers (PMID: 31809852).
Acebutolol, atenolol, bisoprolol, esmolol, and metoprolol are second generation beta1-selective blockers (PMID: 31809852).
Carteolol, carvedilol, and labetalol are non-selective third generation beta-blockers (PMID: 31809852).
Betaxolol, celiprolol, and nebivolol are third generation beta1-selective blockers (PMID: 31809852).
In addition to their beta-blocking action, however, propranolol and timolol have high affinity for 5-hydroxytryptamine (serotonin or 5-HT) receptors, namely 5HT2B and 5HT2C, which play a pivotal role in the pathophysiology of migraine via 5-HT synthesis. It has been shown that beta-blockers with intrinsic sympathomimetic activity (i.e., acebutolol, oxprenolol, pindolol) are not as effective in migraine prevention (PMID: 31809852).
Some of the beta-blockers, first of all pindolol, but also acebutolol, carteolol and celiprolol, are capable of stimulating beta-1 receptors in the absence of catecholamine. These are partial agonists with intrinsic sympathomimetic activity that become functional antagonists in the presence of high concentrations of noradrenaline and adrenaline (PMID: 31809852).
Arbutamine, a new potent non-selective beta-adrenoceptor agonist with mild alpha 1-sympathomimetic activity, has been developed specifically for pharmacological stress testing (PMID: 9183607).
The inotropic activity of dobutamine has previously been attributed to selective stimulation of myocardial beta 1-adrenoceptors. However, recent studies from a number of laboratories indicate that the mechanism of action of dobutamine is substantially more complex. Dobutamine has the capacity to stimulate beta 1-, beta 2-, and alpha 1-adrenoceptors in the cardiovascular system at doses that approximate those used clinically. It has recently been suggested that the inotropic activity of dobutamine results from combined beta 1- and alpha 1-adrenoceptor stimulation in the myocardium, and that this activity could explain, at least in part, the inotropic selectivity of the compound (PMID: 3310640).
Epinephrine and norepinephrine are non-selective adrenic receptor agonists, their actions result from the activation of nine different adrenoreceptors (PMID: 30740663).
Dopamine is an immediate precursor of norepinephrine and epinephrine (PMID: 32473788).
L-threo-3,4-dihydroxyphenylserine (L-DOPS, droxidopa) is a synthetic catecholamino acid. When taken orally, L-DOPS is converted to the sympathetic neurotransmitter, norepinephrine (NE), via decarboxylation catalyzed by L-aromatic-amino-acid decarboxylase (LAAAD) (PMID: 17214596).
Isoprenaline is a non-selective beta-receptor agonist, lacking alpha-agonist effect (PMID: 27919274).
Metipranolol and levobunolol are non-cardio-selective beta-adrenoceptor antagonists (PMID: 2883990).
Bupranolol is a beta1- and beta2-blocking drug with some intrinsic sympathomimetic and local anesthetic activity (PMID: 3951800).
Landiolol is an ultra-short-acting intravenous beta1-blocker (PMID: 38045455).
Propafenone is acting as a non-selective beta-blocker (PMID: 12395362).
Sotalol, timolol, propranolol, and carvedilol are nonselective beta-blockers (PMID: 37885367).

Pazopanib (GW786034) is a multitargeted tyrosine kinase inhibitor against VEGFR-1, -2, and -3, PDGFR-A, -B, and c-Kit. Pazopanib binds to the ATP pocket of the tyrosine kinase on the internal domain of the receptor, inhibiting activation and downstream VEGFR signaling (PMID: 23359171).
Sunitinib (SU11248) is a multitargeted tyrosine kinase inhibitor of VEGFR-1, -2, -3, PDGFRs, KIT, FLT3, RET and CSF-1R. Sunitinib binds to the ATP pocket of the tyrosine kinase on the internal domain of the receptor, inhibiting activation and downstream VEGFR signaling (PMID: 23359171).
Nintedanib (BIBF 1120) is a multitargeted tyrosine kinase inhibitor which simultaneously acts on three key receptor families involved in angiogenesis: VEGFR1-3, PDGFRA,-B and FGFR1-4. Nintedanib binds to the ATP pocket of the tyrosine kinase on the internal domain of the receptor, inhibiting activation and downstream VEGFR signaling (PMID: 18559524, 23359171).
Aflibercept forms a homogenous 1:1 complex with multiple VEGFR1 and VEGFR2 ligands, including VEGF-A, -B, -C, -D and PlGF thereby blocking not only the amino acids necessary for VEGFR1/R2 binding but also occludes the heparin-binding site on VEGF165 (PMID: 38239196; 27234973).

10537	NUP214-ABL1(fusion kinase)-NUP155 complex		Human	ALL-SIL cell line, K-562 cell line, KE-37 cell line, HEK293T cells	23872305	The oncogenic NUP214-ABL1 fusion kinase is a constitutively active protein tyrosine kinase that is found in 6% of patients with T-cell acute lymphoblastic leukemia and that promotes proliferation and survival of T-lymphoblasts. The kinase activation of NUP214-ABL1 depends on its localization at the nuclear pore complex. Three NUP214-ABL1-interacting proteins, MAD2L1, NUP155, and SMC4, are strictly required for the proliferation and survival of NUP214-ABL1-positive T-cell acute lymphoblastic leukemia cells (PMID: 23872305). The NUP214-ABL1 fusion protein is involved in T-cell acute lymphoblastic leukemia (T-ALL) (PMID: 23872305).	The oncogenic NUP214-ABL1 fusion kinase is sensitive to imatinib and proliferation of cell lines expressing NUP214-ABL1 is inhibited by imatinib. The multi-kinase inhibitors dasatinib and bosutinib inhibit both ABL and SRC kinases and are used for the treatment of imatinib-resistant and -sensitive BCR-ABL-positive malignancies. 10541	AGTR2-DRD1 complex		Human	renal proximal tubule cells (nRPTC); HEK-293 cells	22710646	In human renal proximal tubule cells, sodium reabsorption is decreased by the dopamine D1-like receptors (D1R/D5) and the angiotensin type 2 receptor (AT2R), whereas the angiotensin type 1 receptor increases sodium reabsorption. Aberrant control of these opposing systems is thought to lead to sodium retention and, subsequently, hypertension. D1Rs and AT2Rs heterodimerized and cooperatively increased cAMP and cGMP production, protein phosphatase 2A activation, sodium-potassium-ATPase internalization, and sodium transport inhibition (PMID: 22710646).			The data suggest that use of an angiotensin type 2 receptor (AT2R) agonist and a method to restore dopamine D1 receptor (D1R) coupling by inhibiting GRK4 expression or providing an increase in proximal tubule cAMP may provide selective antihypertensive therapy. Similarly, the combination of a D1R agonist and an AT1R antagonist may provide an alternative therapeutic approach (PMID: 22710646). 10587	GABRA3-GABRB1-GABRE complex		Human		16412217	"The A-type receptors for gamma-aminobutyric acid (GABAA) mediate the majority of fast inhibitory transmission in the mammalian central nervous system. 
The GABA sensitivity of the receptors varies by a factor of 100, with the alpha3beta1epsilon (GABRA2-GABRB1-GABRE) subtype exhibiting the greatest sensitivity and the alpha3beta1gamma2 (GABRA3-GABRB1-GABRG2) subtype exhibiting the least sensitivity."	GABAA receptors are pentameric ligand-gated ion-channels, composed of subunits from many subunit classes: alpha1-6, beta1-3, gamma1-3, delta, epsilon, theta, pi, and rho1-3. "X-linked nephrogenic diabetes insipidus (NDI) in humans is frequently caused by misfolded, traffic-defective mutants of the vasopressin V2 receptor (V2R). It has been shown that distinct cell membrane permeable antagonists may rescue function in vitro of several of these mutant V2Rs. For example, the nonpeptide antagonists SR49059, OPC31260, OPC41061 (tolvaptan), and SR121463B (satavaptan) were able to induce maturation and basolateral membrane localization and function in eight out of nine V2R mutants in stably
transfected MDCK cells. Another example is the aminoglycoside antibiotic (G418) which rescued a V2R mutant with a premature truncation causing X-linked NDI; addition of this antibiotic to kidney collecting duct cells expressing the E242X V2R mutant increased arginine vasopressin-stimulated cAMP responses. In mutant E242X mice, the G418 compound suppressed the premature stop codon, facilitating protein translation to continue the normal end of the gene, leading to improved urine-concentrating ability. In an in vivo proof-of-principle study, the effect of the peptidomimetic V1AR/V2R antagonist SR49059 to rescue function of R137H, W164S, and des185-193 V2R mutants in patients with NDI was studied. A significant drop in urine production and water intake concurrent with a significant increase in urine osmolarity in response to this particular compound occurred in a subset of patients with NDI. Clinical rescue of functional mutant V2Rs at clinically safe, feasible concentrations has been reported to be most effective with OPC31260 and OPC41061; these compounds are promising candidates to ameliorate the alterations of NDI (PMID: 34830210)." Type 2 bradykinin receptor (B2R) is an essential G protein-coupled receptor (GPCR) that regulates the cardiovascular system as a vasodepressor. Icatibant is a selective, competitive antagonist to bradykinin (BK) against its binding to the bradykinin B2 receptor. 10657	DRD1-DRD2 complex	D1R-D2R complex; dopamine D1/D2 receptor heteromer	Human	 post-mortem striatal tissues	21113156	"The dopamine D1-D2 receptor complex induces calcium release via a Gq-dependent pathway distinct from Gs/Golf- or Gi/Go-dependent pathways activated by D1R or D2R independently. In rats administration of an interfering peptide that disrupts the D1-D2 receptor complex substantially reduced immobility in the forced swim test (FST) without affecting locomotor activity, and decreased escape failures in learned helplessness tests in rats (PMID: 21113156).
In rats, the sex difference in D1-D2 levels occurred even though D1 receptor expression was lower in female than in male with no difference in D2 receptor expression. Analysis of signaling pathways revealed that the sex difference in D1-D2 heteromer expression led to differences in basal and heteromer-stimulated activities of two important signaling pathways, BDNF/TrkB and Akt/GSK3/beta-catenin (PMID: 32087746).
Pharmacological analysis together with a highly selective interfering peptide further showed that the D1-D2 receptor complex had signaling characteristics distinct from its constituent D1 or D2 receptors, being coupled to the Gq protein with the promotion of intracellular calcium signaling through activation of phospholipase C. The behavioral consequences of D1–D2 receptor heteromer disruption was in and of itself reward enhancing. D1-D2 receptor heteromer disruption also augmented cocaine reward, and led to
the promotion, exacerbation and acceleration of the locomotor activating and incentive motivational effects associated with cocaine. The present findings indicate that a role of the D1-D2 heteromer is to exert tonic inhibition on brain reward mechanisms and thus function as a brake to constrain the development and expression of addiction-like behaviors, a finding that would have significance in humans given the identification of D1-D2 heteromers in human striatum. Expression of the D1-D2 heteromer was reduced in adolescent rat NAc suggesting a possible involvement in adolescent cocaine addiction vulnerability through amplification of the rewarding effects of the drug (PMID: 27480020).

10698	D2 dopamine receptor	DRD2 homodimer	Human	 HEK-293 cells; CHO-K1 cells 	17706924			Increased D2 dopamine receptor homodimer formation has been associated with development of schizophrenia (PMID: 30987329).	"Aripiprazole is the first next-generation atypical antipsychotic with a mechanism of action that differs from currently marketed typical and atypical antipsychotics. Aripiprazole displays properties of an agonist and antagonist in animal models of dopaminergic hypoactivity and hyperactivity, respectively. The results, together with previous studies demonstrating partial agonist activity at serotonin 5-hydroxytryptamine (5-HT)1A receptors and antagonist activity at 5-HT2A receptors, support the identification of aripiprazole as a dopamine-serotonin system stabilizer (PMID: 12065741).
Brexpiprazole is an oral atypical antipsychotic agent approved for the treatment of schizophrenia in the EU (in adult patients) and the USA, as well as in some other countries, including Japan. Like aripiprazole, it is a partial agonist at dopamine D2 and serotonin 5-HT1A receptors and an antagonist at serotonin 5-HT2A receptors (PMID: 30671869).
Cariprazine is a dopamine D3 and D2 receptor partial agonist, with a preference for the D3 receptor. Cariprazine is also a partial agonist at the serotonin 5-HT1A receptor and acts as an antagonist at 5-HT2B and 5-HT2A receptors (PMID: 27440212).
Aripiprazole lauroxil is a long-acting intramuscular injection that works as a combination of partial agonist activity at D2 and 5-HT1A receptors combined with antagonist activity at 5-HT2A receptors (PMID: 34287335).
Blonanserin is an atypical antipsychotic agent with dopamine D(2)/serotonin 5-HT(2A) antagonistic properties (PMID: 22691713).
Atypical or second-generation antipsychotics, such as Risperidone and Clozapine predominantly block dopaminergic D2 and serotonin receptor 2A (5-HT2A) neurotransmission (PMID: 38387714).
Dopamine D2 receptors (D2R) are known to form transient homodimer complexes, of which the increased formation has already been associated with development of schizophrenia.  Agonist addition has shown to prolong the D2R dimer lifetime and increase the level of dimer formation. D2R antagonists, such as clozapine, risperidone, and droperidol, and the D2R agonist quinpirole did not significantly modify dimer formation (PMID: 30987329).
Antipsychotic drugs (APDs) used in the treatment of schizophrenia may be classified as typical or atypical APDs. Atypical APDs elicit fewer extrapyramidal symptoms (EPS) than typical APDs at clinically equivalent dosages. The atypical APDs also have other advantages, e.g. the ability to improve cognition and a greater antidepressant action. Most of the available atypical APDs (clozapine, quetiapine, risperidone, olanzapine, and ziprasidone), as well as some of those in development, e.g. iloperidone, ORG-5222, perospirone, and blonanserin, are more potent antagonists of serotonin (5-HT)2A receptors compared to their ability to antagonize dopamine (DA) D2 receptors (PMID: 12664192).
Sertindole is an antipsychotic drug with high affinity for dopamine D2, alpha-1-adrenoceptors and serotonin 5-HT2A and 5-HT2c receptors. The 5-HT2c receptor component of sertindole may be clinically relevant as this receptor subtype is implicated in regulation of anxiety, cognition/memory and brain plasticity (PMID: 11594443).
Spiperone is a widely used pharmacological tool that acts as a potent dopamine D2, serotonin 5-HT1A, and serotonin 5-HT2A antagonist. Although spiperone also binds at 5-HT2C receptors, it is one of the very few agents that display some (ca. 1000-fold) binding selectivity for 5-HT2A versus 5-HT2C receptors (PMID: 9836624).
Asenapine is a new atypical antipsychotic medication with high affinity for dopamine D2 and 5HT2A receptors that has been approved by the FDA in adults for the acute treatment of schizophrenia in the USA. Asenapine acts as an dopamine D2, 5HT2A, HT2C, and 5HT7 antagonist (PMID: 20642375).
Paliperidone extended-release tablet (paliperidone ER) is a centrally active dopamine D(2)- and serotonergic 5-HT(2A)-receptor antagonist that is registered for the treatment of schizophrenia (PMID: 19713555).
Lurasidone has antagonistic effects on the dopamine D2, 5-hydroxytryptamine (5-HT)2A, and 5-HT7 receptors and a partial agonistic effect on the 5-HT1A receptor with low affinities for muscarinic M1, histamine H1, and a1 adrenergic receptors (PMID: 37789971).
Paliperidone palmitate is the palmitate ester of paliperidone, the major metabolite of risperidone, and is formulated as a long-acting injection for intramuscular use. Its pharmacology is comparable to risperidone, having D2 and 5-HT(2A) receptor antagonist activity (PMID: 18973393).
Lumateperone acts syn-ergistically through multiple systems (serotonergic, dopaminergic and glutamatergic), thus representing a unique approach for the therapeutic management of a range of neuropsychiatric disorders. It possesses a potent antagonistic activity at 5-hydroxytryptamine (serotonin) 2A (5-HT2A) receptors and also binds to dopamine (D1, D2) receptors with partial agonism at presynaptic D2 receptors and postsynaptic antagonism. Further, preclinical data demonstrated that lumateperone uniquely acts as an indirect modulator of glutamatergic phosphoprotein with D1-dependent augmentation of both NMDA and AMPA activity via the mammalian target of rapamycin (mTOR) pathway, mechanisms thought to predict potent and rapid antidepressant effects (PMID: 30596390).
Amisulpride, a benzamide derivative, is an antipsychotic drug with a pharmacological profile distinct from that of classical neuroleptics such as haloperidol and from that of another benzamide, remoxipride. Amisulpride has presynaptic D2/D3 dopamine receptor antagonist activity and limbic selectivity. The pharmacological profile of amisulpride, characterized by a preferential blockade of effects involving presynaptic mechanisms and limbic structures, may explain the clinical efficacy of this drug against both negative and positive symptoms of schizophrenia and its low propensity to produce extrapyramidal side effects (PMID: 8996184).
The D2/D3 agonist quinpirole, which induces receptor internalization in vitro, was administered at graded doses in non-human primates while imaging with simultaneous positron emission tomography (PET) and functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI). A pronounced temporal divergence between receptor occupancy and fMRI signal was observed: occupancy remained elevated while fMRI responded transiently. Analogous experiments with an D2/D3 antagonist (prochlorperazine) and a lower-affinity D2/D3 agonist (ropinirole) exhibited reduced temporal dissociation between occupancy and function, consistent with a mechanism of desensitization and internalization that depends upon drug efficacy and affinity (PMID: 26388148).
Chronic treatment with dopamine (DA) receptor antagonists such as D2 antagonist haloperidol (Haldol) and other first-generation antipsychotics in schizophrenic patients is relatively unsuccessful at treating negative symptoms such as lack of energy, fatigue, and avolition. In fact, drugs such as haloperidol can induce
negative symptoms in healthy volunteers, including avolition. In addition to physical symptoms of fatigue and amotivation in schizophrenic patients, clinical reports indicate that chronic exposure to antipsychotics is often associated with adverse side effects such as dystonia, extrapyramidal symptoms, and sedation. Treatment compliance issues are at the forefront of schizophrenia and other psychiatric disorders due to undesirable side effects, impaired cognition, and/or a general lack of insight, which may ultimately lead to severe negative consequences. For these reasons, it has become increasingly common for clinicians to prescribe long-acting injectable antipsychotics, including haloperidol decanoate, which is a depot formulation of the DA D2 antagonist (PMID: 37615683).
Zuclopenthixol is a mixed D1/D2 dopamine receptor antagonist (PMID: 1822319).
The dopamine receptor D2 antagonist trifluoperazine HCl inhibits growth and proliferation of glioblastoma (GBM) cells in a dose dependent manner. Trifluoperazine's inhibition of GBM cells is cell line dependent and correlates with variations in dopamine receptor expression profile. Thus components of the dopamine receptor signaling pathways are potential targets for pharmacological interventions of GBM growth (PMID: 29066348).
The dopamine D2 receptor blocker thioridazine induces cell death in human uterine cervical carcinoma cell line SiHa (PMID: 25832589).
sulpiride is a dopamine D2 receptor blocker (PMID: 33811308).
Rotigotine is a nonergolinic dopamine D3/D2/D1 receptor agonist delivered via a transdermal system and has been evaluated for the treatment of idiopathic Parkinson's disease (PMID: 16268667).
Fibromyalgia (FM) is a complex pathology described as persistent hyperalgesia including somatic and mood dysfunctions, depression and anxiety. Although the etiology of FM is still unknown, a significant decrease in biogenic amines is a common characteristic in its pathogenesis. The study investigated the role of dopamine D3/D2 receptor during the reserpine-induced pain in mice. Pramipexole (PPX) - a dopaminergic D3/D2 receptor agonist - inhibited mechanical allodynia and thermal sensitivity induced by reserpine. Reserpine administration induced significant downregulation of dopamine concentration in the central nervous system, and repeated treatment with PPX restored dopamine levels in the frontal cortex and spinal cord tissues. PPX treatment inhibited oxidants production such as DCFH (2',7'-dichlorodihydrofluorescein) and nitrite, also decreased oxidative damage (carbonyl), and upregulated the activity of superoxide dismutase in the spinal cord. Together, our findings demonstrated the ability of dopamine D3/D2 receptor-preferring agonist in reducing pain and mood dysfunction allied to FM in mice (PMID: 34269222).
Piribedil acts as a non-ergot partial dopamine D2/D3-selective agonist, blocks alpha2-adrenoreceptors and has minimal effects on serotoninergic, cholinergic, and histaminergic receptors. Animal models support the efficacy of piribedil to improve parkinsonian motor symptoms with a lower propensity than levodopa to induce dyskinesia. In Parkinson disease (PD) patients, randomized double-blind studies show that piribedil (150-300 mg/day, three times daily) is superior to placebo in improving motor disability in early PD patients (PMID: 27344665).
Pimozide is a conventional antipsychotic drug largely used in the therapy for schizophrenia and Tourette's syndrome. Pimozide is assumed to inhibit synaptic transmission at the CNS by acting as a dopaminergic D2 receptor antagonist (PMID: 36831024).
Glioblastoma (GBM), a primary malignant brain tumor, has a poor prognosis, even with standard treatments such as radiotherapy and chemotherapy. This study explored the anticancer effects of the synergistic combination of perphenazine (PER), a dopamine receptor D2/3 (DRD2/3) antagonist, and temozolomide (TMZ), a standard treatment for GBM, in patient-derived human GBM tumorspheres (TSs). Synergistic combination of perphenazine and temozolomide suppresses patient-derived glioblastoma tumorspheres (PMID: 39392921).
Pergolide is a potent, direct-acting dopamine D1/D2 agonist used in treating Parkinson's disease (PMID: 1832202).
Neuroleptic drug molindone hydrochloride is a dopamine D2/D5 receptor antagonist and it is in late stage development for the treatment of impulsive aggression in children and adolescents who have attention deficient/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) (PMID: 28142338).
Neuroleptic-induced tardive dyskinesia (TD) continues to be a serious problem in the psychopharmacology of schizophrenia. Metoclopramide, a dopamine D2-receptor blocker commonly used in non-psychiatric medical patients, can also produce persistent TD (PMID: 8100643).
Fluphenazine is a potent antipsychotic drug used to treat schizophrenia and other psychotic symptoms. Its clinical benefit is mainly mediated by the antagonism of dopamine D2 receptors (PMID: 17891479).
flupentixol is a D1/D2 dopamine receptor antagonist (PMID: 38125760).
Domperidone, a dopamine receptor D2 antagonist, induces apoptosis by inhibiting the ERK/STAT3-mediated pathway in human colon cancer HCT116 Cells (PMID: 38125760).
Chlorpromazine (CPZ), a dopaminergic D2 receptor antagonist and schizophrenia therapy, was proposed to exert antiinflammatory effects in the central nervous system. The study show sthat CPZ lessens Kv1.3 channel activity and reduces proinflammatory cytokine production (PMID: 39435609). 
Cabergoline, a dopamine D2 receptor agonist, prevents neuronal cell death under oxidative stress via reducing excitotoxicity (PMID: 24914776).
Bromocriptine is a sympatholytic, D2-dopamine receptor agonist for the treatment of type 2 diabetes (PMID: 21447659).
Apomorphine (APO) is a potent D1 and D2 dopamine agonist (PMID: 26037961).
The study analysed the effects of dopamine receptor agonists and antagonists on rat gastrointestinal transit (GIT) in an attempt to identify the mechanisms involved. Dopamine (DA), apomorphine, quinpirole, bromocriptine and fenoldopam were given by subcutaneous (s.c.), intrathecal (i.t.), intracisternal (i.c.) and/or intraperitoneal (i.p.) routes. In general, DA (200 micrograms, i.t.), apomorphine (3, 5 and 10 mg/kg, s.c.; or 10, 30 and 100 micrograms, i.t.), and bromocriptine (1, 5 and 10 mg/kg, s.c.) elicited decreases in gastrointestinal transit which were significantly antagonized by the D2 receptor antagonists domperidone or alizapride (both 5 mg/kg, s.c.), but remained unaffected by the D1 receptor antagonist SCH 23390 (5 mg/kg, s.c.) 10709	5-hydroxytryptamine receptor 2A	HTR2A homodimer	Human	HEK293 cells	20831885				"Aripiprazole is the first next-generation atypical antipsychotic with a mechanism of action that differs from currently marketed typical and atypical antipsychotics. Aripiprazole displays properties of an agonist and antagonist in animal models of dopaminergic hypoactivity and hyperactivity, respectively. The results, together with previous studies demonstrating partial agonist activity at serotonin 5-hydroxytryptamine (5-HT)1A receptors and antagonist activity at 5-HT2A receptors, support the identification of aripiprazole as a dopamine-serotonin system stabilizer (PMID: 12065741).
Brexpiprazole is an oral atypical antipsychotic agent approved for the treatment of schizophrenia in the EU (in adult patients) and the USA, as well as in some other countries, including Japan. Like aripiprazole, it is a partial agonist at dopamine D2 and serotonin 5-HT1A receptors and an antagonist at serotonin 5-HT2A receptors (PMID: 30671869).
At clinically relevant doses, flibanserin acts predominantly at 5-HT(1A) receptors as an agonist and secondarily at 5-HT(2A) receptors as an antagonist (PMID: 20840530).
Cariprazine is a dopamine D3 and D2 receptor partial agonist, with a preference for the D3 receptor. Cariprazine is also a partial agonist at the serotonin 5-HT1A receptor and acts as an antagonist at 5-HT2B and 5-HT2A receptors (PMID: 27440212).
Aripiprazole lauroxil is a long-acting intramuscular injection that works as a combination of partial agonist activity at D2 and 5-HT1A receptors combined with antagonist activity at 5-HT2A receptors (PMID: 34287335).
Blonanserin is an atypical antipsychotic agent with dopamine D(2)/serotonin 5-HT(2A) antagonistic properties (PMID: 22691713).
Atypical or second-generation antipsychotics, such as Risperidone and Clozapine predominantly block dopaminergic D2 and serotonin receptor 2A (5-HT2A) neurotransmission (PMID: 38387714).
TNX-102 SL is a bedtime sublingual formulation of cyclobenzaprine with potent binding and antagonist activity at 5-HT2A, alpha1-adrenergic, H1 histaminergic, and M1 muscarinic receptors, which play roles in the pharmacological management of sleep disturbances (PMID: 38350291).
Blockage of 5-HT2A receptors with ketanserin or droperidol induces a weak anti-asthmatic effect (PMID: 10637649).
Antipsychotic drugs (APDs) used in the treatment of schizophrenia may be classified as typical or atypical APDs. Atypical APDs elicit fewer extrapyramidal symptoms (EPS) than typical APDs at clinically equivalent dosages. The atypical APDs also have other advantages, e.g. the ability to improve cognition and a greater antidepressant action. Most of the available atypical APDs (clozapine, quetiapine, risperidone, olanzapine, and ziprasidone), as well as some of those in development, e.g. iloperidone, ORG-5222, perospirone, and blonanserin, are more potent antagonists of serotonin (5-HT)2A receptors compared to their ability to antagonize dopamine (DA) D2 receptors (PMID: 12664192).
Antipsychotic-induced akathisia can be difficult to manage and may respond to mirtazapine based on its antagonist activity at the serotonin 5-HT(2A)/5-HT(2C) receptors (PMID: 18460588).
Nefazodone (NEF), a 5-HT2A/2C antagonist antidepressant, is extensively metabolized in the human body to hydroxy NEF (OH-NEF), p-hydroxy NEF (pOH-NEF), a dione metabolite, and via cleavage of the molecule to m-chlorophenyl-piperazine (mCPP) and BMY-33604 (PMID: 8730981).
Sertindole is an antipsychotic drug with high affinity for dopamine D2, alpha-1-adrenoceptors and serotonin 5-HT2A and 5-HT2c receptors. The 5-HT2c receptor component of sertindole may be clinically relevant as this receptor subtype is implicated in regulation of anxiety, cognition/memory and brain plasticity (PMID: 11594443).
Spiperone is a widely used pharmacological tool that acts as a potent dopamine D2, serotonin 5-HT1A, and serotonin 5-HT2A antagonist. Although spiperone also binds at 5-HT2C receptors, it is one of the very few agents that display some (ca. 1000-fold) binding selectivity for 5-HT2A versus 5-HT2C receptors (PMID: 9836624).
 At h5-HT2A receptors, terguride, lisuride, bromocriptine, cabergoline, and pergolide displayed potent agonist properties, whereas apomorphine and roxindole were antagonists and piribedil was inactive. Only pergolide and cabergoline displayed pronounced agonist properties at h5-HT2B receptors. At 5-HT2C receptors, lisuride, bromocriptine, pergolide, and cabergoline were efficacious agonists, apomorphine and terguride were antagonists, and piribedil was inactive (PMID: 12388668).
The antidepressant trazodone is a 5-HT 2A/2C receptor antagonist (PMID: 15614572).
Asenapine is a new atypical antipsychotic medication with high affinity for dopamine D2 and 5HT2A receptors that has been approved by the FDA in adults for the acute treatment of schizophrenia in the USA. Asenapine acts as an dopamine D2, 5HT2A, HT2C, and 5HT7 antagonist (PMID: 20642375).
Paliperidone extended-release tablet (paliperidone ER) is a centrally active dopamine D(2)- and serotonergic 5-HT(2A)-receptor antagonist that is registered for the treatment of schizophrenia (PMID: 19713555).
Lurasidone has antagonistic effects on the dopamine D2, 5-hydroxytryptamine (5-HT)2A, and 5-HT7 receptors and a partial agonistic effect on the 5-HT1A receptor with low affinities for muscarinic M1, histamine H1, and a1 adrenergic receptors (PMID: 37789971).
Paliperidone palmitate is the palmitate ester of paliperidone, the major metabolite of risperidone, and is formulated as a long-acting injection for intramuscular use. Its pharmacology is comparable to risperidone, having D2 and 5-HT(2A) receptor antagonist activity (PMID: 18973393).
Pimavanserin, a 5-hydroxytryptamine 2A receptor inverse agonist, reverses prepulse inhibition deficits in the nucleus accumbens and ventral hippocampus (PMID: 34666074).
Lumateperone acts syn-ergistically through multiple systems (serotonergic, dopaminergic and glutamatergic), thus representing a unique approach for the therapeutic management of a range of neuropsychiatric disorders. It possesses a potent antagonistic activity at 5-hydroxytryptamine (serotonin) 2A (5-HT2A) receptors and also binds to dopamine (D1, D2) receptors with partial agonism at presynaptic D2 receptors and postsynaptic antagonism. Further, preclinical data demonstrated that lumateperone uniquely acts as an indirect modulator of glutamatergic phosphoprotein with D1-dependent augmentation of both NMDA and AMPA activity via the mammalian target of rapamycin (mTOR) pathway, mechanisms thought to predict potent and rapid antidepressant effects (PMID: 30596390)." Bevacizumab binds to all isoforms of VEGFA. A single bevacizumab molecule can bind both active sites in a single VEGFA dimer and prevents interaction with VEGFR-1 and VEGFR-2 (PMID: 27234973; 24445500).
The tyrosine kinase inhibitor axitinib is a selective inhibitor of VEGFR-1 (FLT1), -2 (KDR) and -3 (FLT4). Binding of axitinib to the kinase domain of VEGF receptors stabilizes an inactive conformation of the kinase, thus inhibiting signal transduction by VEGF (PMID: 19876699). 
Pazopanib (GW786034), is a multitargeted tyrosine kinase inhibitor targeting VEGFR-1, -2, and -3, PDGFR-A, -B, and c-Kit. Pazopanib binds to the ATP pocket of the tyrosine kinase on the internal domain of the receptor, inhibiting activation and downstream VEGFR signaling (PMID: 23359171). 
Sunitinib (SU11248) is a multitargeted tyrosine kinase inhibitor of VEGFR-1, -2, -3, PDGFRs, KIT, FLT3, RET and CSF-1R. Sunitinib binds to the ATP pocket of the tyrosine kinase on the internal domain of the receptor, inhibiting activation and downstream VEGFR signaling (PMID: 23359171). 
The anti-angiogenic factor sorafenib targets VEGFR1, -2, and -3 as well as c-Kit, FLT3, GDNF and PDGFR-beta to inhibit VEGF-induced signaling (PMID: 38239196).
Nintedanib (BIBF 1120) is a multitargeted tyrosine kinase inhibitor which simultaneously acts on three key receptor families involved in angiogenesis: VEGFR1-3, PDGFRA,-B and FGFR1-4. Nintedanib binds to the ATP pocket of the tyrosine kinase on the internal domain of the receptor, inhibiting activation and downstream VEGFR signaling (PMID: 18559524, 23359171)." 10725	Muscarinic acetylcholine receptor M3	CHRM3 homodimer	Human	HEK293 cells	16368694	"M1, M2, and M3 muscarinic acetylcholine receptors (mAChR) can form constitutive homo- and heterodimers in living HEK293 cells expressing physiological levels of these receptors. Short term agonist treatment did not modify the oligomeric status of homo- and heterodimers (PMID: 16368694).
Most of the cholinergic components which are expressed in neurons (e.g. acetylcholine, choline acetyltransferase, high affinity choline transporter, muscarinic and nicotinic acetylcholine receptors and acetylcholinesterase) are also present in lymphocytic cells, thus constituting an independent cholinergic system that can be regulated in an autocrine fashion. Both T- and B-cells naturally express high levels of M3, M4, and M5 muscarinic acetylcholine receptors. Stimulation of T and B cells with muscarinic receptor agonists elicits intracellular calcium signaling, up-regulates of c-Fos expression, and increases nitric oxide synthesis and cytokine production (PMID: 20398705)."		"CHRM3 was upregulated in clinical prostate cancer tissues compared with adjacent non-cancer tissues (PMID: 26071486).
"	"Methanthelinium binds competitively and non-selectively to all five human muscarinic acetylcholine receptor subtypes with nanomolar affinity and is able to functionally inhibit ACh responses in a competitive fashion, with a slight subtype preference for M1 and M4 (PMID: 29938305).
Glycopyrrolate (glycopyrronium bromide), a quaternary ammonium compound, is a muscarinic receptor antagonist which has been used in pre-anaesthetic medication to reduce gastric acid and salivary secretions or to reverse neuromuscular blockade. Glycopyrrolate has been used as a bronchodilator in patients with asthma and COPD (PMID: 10385241).
Revefenacin is a potent and selective antagonist with similar affinity for the different subtypes of muscarinic receptors (M1-M5).  Revefenacin treatment delivered via nebulization led to improvements in lung function in patients with COPD (PMID: 33821890).
Fesoterodine is a muscarinic receptor antagonist with high and nearly equal affinity for both the M2 and M3 muscarinic receptors, poor penetration of the blood-brain barrier, lack of hepatic first-pass activation -fesoterodine being rapidly and extensively converted to its active metabolite, 5-hydroxymethyl tolterodine, by ubiquitous esterases-, and its extended-release formulation. Fesoterodine's pharmacological profile is optimal for the treatment of overactive bladder (PMID: 29803689).
Trospium is an oral pan-muscarinic receptor antagonist that is approved for the treatment of overactive bladder. Its highly polar tertiary amine structure prevents it from reaching detectable levels in the cerebrospinal fluid and should obviate adverse central nervous system effects (PMID: 33626254).
Tolterodine and solifenacin are antimuscarinic agents developed for the treatment of overactive bladder (OAB) (PMID: 20970066).
Atropine, propantheline, and oxyphencyclimine are anticholinergic agents. The acid secretion of the nervous phase of gastric secretion was inhibited by the anticholinergic drugs. They influenced gastric secretion to a greater extent than saliva flow. Both propantheline and oxyphencyclimine have a selective action on the stomach superior to atropine (PMID: 14486841).
Solanaceaeous plants such as Atropa, Datura, Duboisia, Hyoscyamus and Scopolia exclusively produce the tropane alkaloids hyoscyamine and scopolamine and are widely used as anticholinergic drugs, which act on the parasympathetic nervous system (PMID: 22305072).
Bethanechol is a direct-acting muscarinic receptor agonist. Oral bethanechol significantly improves contraction pressures and bolus transit in the smooth muscle portion of the esophagus in patients with severe ineffective esophageal motility (IEM) (PMID: 17413603).
Anisotropine methyl bromide (octatropine methylbromide), an anticholinergic drug, suppresses gastric acid secretion through the night without significant side effects (PMID: 353090).
Cevimeline is a potent direct-acting muscarinic receptor agonist. The major mechanism of action of this muscarinic agonist is increased secretion of exocrine glands, such as salivary and sweat glands and increased tone of the smooth muscle in the gastrointestinal and urinary tract (PMID: 34445613).
Clidinium bromide (N-methyl-quinuclidinyl-benzylate) is a rarely used antimuscarinic drug that is marketed in combination with chlordiazepoxide as an antispasmodic for use in irritable bowel syndrome (PMID: 19465630).
The orthosteric antagonist N-methylscopolamine (NMS) binds to the binding pocket of the muscarinic acetylcholine receptor formed by transmembrane alpha-helices (PMID: 28091608).
Oxybutynin, tolterodine, darifenacin, solifenacin and trospium are the five major antimuscarinics approved for the treatment of overactive bladder (OAB) (PMID: 16465186).
The M3 muscarinic acetylcholine receptor (M3R), a member of the G-protein coupled receptor superfamily, encoded by the CHRM3 gene, in cardiac function and the regulation of blood pressure (PMID: 38010846).
Overexpression of CHRM3 or activation of CHRM3 by carbachol promoted cell proliferation, migration, and castration resistance in prostate cancer. On the contrary, blockading CHRM3 by shRNA or treatment with darifenacin inhibited prostate cancer growth and castration resistance both in vitro and in vivo (PMID: 26071486).
Mydriatic medications dilate the pupil to allow examination of the retina. Mydriasis is typically accomplished using a combination of topical phenylephrine, a potent alpha-receptor agonist, and cyclopentolate, an anticholinergic (PMID: 36868806).
Although ipratropium is a non-selective anti-muscarinic agent, its effect in the lungs is mediated largely through the M3 receptor, which upon activation causes smooth muscle contraction (PMID: 28461224).
Methacholine is a non-selective muscarinic receptor agonist causing bronchoconstriction (PMID: 27401374).
Pilocarpine is a prototypical drug used to treat glaucoma and dry mouth and is classified as either a full or partial muscarinic agonist. Pilocarpine can act as either an agonist or antagonist of M3 muscarinic acetylcholine receptor, depending on the cell type, expression level, and signaling pathway downstream of this receptor (PMID: 28893976).
Tiotropium bromide is an anticholinergic bronchodilator that is inhaled once daily by patients with COPD and its effect is mediated through a prolonged M3 muscarinic receptor antagonism (PMID: 17127817).
Aclidinium bromide, a muscarinic acetylcholine M3 receptor antagonist, has anti-tumoral properties in several tumors, namely gastric cancer and glioma. Aclidinium bromide might inhibit osteosarcoma cell growth by regulating the PI3K/AKT signaling pathway, which suggests aclidinium bromide is a potential chemotherapeutic agent for osteosarcoma (PMID: 30657552).
Activation of muscarinic subtype 3 (M3) muscarinic cholinergic receptors (mAChRs) increases airway tone, whereas its blockade improves lung function and quality of life in patients with pulmonary diseases. Umeclidinium is a long-acting, inhaled antagonist of the muscarinic cholinergic receptors for treatment of pulmonary diseases (PMID: 23435542).
Imidafenacin is one of the long-acting muscarinic receptor antagonists (LAMAs) with high affinity for the M3 and M1 muscarinic receptor subtypes and low affinity for the M2 subtype. The M3 subtype is expressed on airway smooth muscle and mediates bronchoconstriction. Imidafenacin, improves pulmonary function In patients with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (PMID: 31571853).
Sofpironium bromide is a topical anticholinergic agent for the treatment of hyperhidrosis. The drug is designed to reduce sweating by inhibiting M3 muscarinic receptors in eccrine glands at the application site (PMID: 33236266)." 10732	CHRM1-DRD2 complex		Human	HEK293T cells	36467044			Parkinson's disease (PD) is a neurodegenerative disorder characterized by motor control deficits, which is associated with the loss of striatal dopaminergic neurons from the substantia nigra. In parallel to dopaminergic denervation, there is an increase of acetylcholine within the striatum, resulting in a striatal dopaminergic-cholinergic neurotransmission imbalance. Currently, available PD pharmacotherapy (e.g., prodopaminergic drugs) does not reinstate the altered dopaminergic-cholinergic balance. In addition, it can eventually elicit cholinergic-related adverse effects (PMID: 32231561).	The study evaluated the functional interplay between both receptors via behavioral studies, by implementing the classical acute reserpine pharmacological animal model of experimental parkinsonism. Reserpinized mice were administered with a D2R-selective agonist (sumanirole) and/or an M1R-selective antagonist (VU0255035), and alterations in PD-related behavioral tasks (i.e., locomotor activity) were evaluated. Importantly, VU0255035 (10 mg/kg) potentiated the antiparkinsonian-like effects (i.e., increased locomotor activity and decreased catalepsy) of an ineffective sumanirole dose (3 mg/kg). The data suggest the existence of putative striatal D2R/M1R heteromers, which might be a relevant target to manage PD motor impairments with fewer adverse effects (PMID: 32231561). LPA receptors form homo- and hetero-dimers within the LPA receptor subgroup and hetero-dimers with other receptors (S1P(1-3) and GPR4) (PMID: 17023202). Lysophosphatidic acid (LPA) and sphingosine-1-phosphate (S1P) are bioactive lysophopholipids involved in diverse biological processes. Investigation of the S1P pathway has led to the approval of three S1PR modulators, fingolimod, siponimod and ozanimod, as medicines for patients with multiple sclerosis (PMID: 33289881).	"Fingolimod is an FDA-approved sphingosine 1-phosphate (S1P) receptor agonist (PMID: 38031996).
Siponimod is a dual agonist at the sphingosine-1 phosphate receptors, S1PR1 and S1PR5 (PMID: 26856814).
These S1PR modulators differ in their affinities for S1PR subtypes. Fingolimod (when phosphorylated) targets four of the receptor subtypes (S1PR1 , S1PR3 , S1PR4 and S1PR5 ), while siponimod and ozanimod target S1PR1 and S1PR5, and ponesimod shows high affinity for S1PR1. Notably, fingolimod is a prodrug and must be phosphorylated by sphingosine kinase before it displays binding affinity for S1PRs (PMID: 33289881)." Selexipag is a selective and orally bioavailable prostacyclin (PGI2 ) receptor (IP receptor) agonist that is approved for the treatment of pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH). Selexipag and its active metabolite ACT-333679 relaxed rings of the isolated rat femoral artery contracted with either prostaglandin F2alpha (PGF2alpha ) or the alpha1 adrenoceptor (alpha1AR) agonist phenylephrine. ACT-333679 also inhibited contraction of the femoral artery to sympathetic nerve stimulation. In contrast, PGI2 analogs (iloprost, beraprost, and treprostinil) caused additional contraction of arterial rings precontracted with phenylephrine, which was reverted to relaxation by antagonism of EP3 receptors. Treprostinil augmented contraction of the femoral artery to sympathetic nerve stimulation in an EP3 receptor-dependent manner. It is concluded that selexipag and ACT-333679 are vasorelaxants of the rat femoral artery and, unlike PGI2 analogs, do not cause paradoxical vasoconstriction via activation of EP3 receptors. EP3 receptor-mediated vasoconstriction may contribute to the well documented peripheral muscle pain reported in patients with PAH receiving PGI2 analogs. Leg pain may be less in patients treated with selexipag (PMID: 29588339).

PGI2 replacement therapy by epoprostenol infusion is one of the best treatments available for PAH (PMID: 25999730)." 10895	PTGFR (variant 1)-PTGFR (variant 4) complex	FP-altFP4 complex; Prostaglandin F2-alpha receptor heterodimer	Human	EK293/EBNA cells	18587449		Prostaglandin F2-alpha receptor gene PTGFR is alternatively spliced, this complex consists of two splice variants: PTGFR variant 1 (wild-type FP) and PTGFR variant 4 (altFP4).	PGF2alpha analogues have been used clinically to reduce ocular hypertension (PMID: 18587449).	"Although PGF2alpha markedly stimulated the wild-type prostaglandin FP receptor (FP), bimatoprost produced not more than a residual effect. Neither PGF2alpha nor bimatoprost activated the altFP4 receptor. In the studies of the kinetic profile for Ca2+ mobilization, prostaglandin F2alpha (PGF2alpha) elicited a rapid increase in intracellular Ca2+ followed by a steady state phase. In contrast, bimatoprost elicited an immediate increase in intracellular Ca2+ followed by a second phase. The prostamide antagonist, AGN211335, selectively and dose-dependently inhibited the bimatoprost-initiated second phase of Ca2+ mobilization, Cyr61 mRNA upregulation and MLC phosphorylation, but did not block the action of PGF2alpha. Bimatoprost lacks effects on the FP receptor but may interact with the FP-altFP receptor heterodimer to induce alterations in second messenger signalling. Hence, FP-altFP complexes may represent the underlying basis of bimatoprost pharmacology (PMID: 18587449).
FDA approved latanoprost, the first FP-related drug for the treatment of glaucoma, in 1996. Because of its high efficiency, it has been the first-line drug against this pathology. Subsequently, similar FP agonists (bimatoprost, travoprost, and tafluprost) were approved (PMID: 36313286).
Latanoprostene bunod is a nitric oxide (NO)-donating prostaglandin F2alpha analogue approved in the USA for the reduction of intraocular pressure (IOP) in patients with open-angle glaucoma (OAG) or ocular hypertension. It is thought to lower IOP by increasing aqueous humour outflow through the uveoscleral pathway (mediated by latanoprost acid) and increasing the facility of aqueous humour outflow through the trabecular meshwork pathway (mediated by NO) (PMID: 29846910).
Carboprost, an analog of prostaglandin F2alpha and an agonist for the prostaglandin F2-alpha receptor (FP receptor), is clinically used to treat postpartum hemorrhage (PPH). However, off-target activation of closely related receptors such as the prostaglandin E receptor subtype EP3 (EP3 receptor) by carboprost results in side effects and limits the clinical application (PMID: 38065938)." 11064	ARRB1-MC1R complex		Human	HEK293 cells	23750009	The melanocortin 1 receptor (MC1R) is a G-protein-coupled receptor (GPCR) crucial for the regulation of melanocyte proliferation and differentiation. MC1R activation by melanocortin hormones triggers the cAMP pathway and stimulates the extracellular-signal-regulated protein kinases ERK1 and ERK2 to promote synthesis of photoprotective eumelanin pigments, among other effects. Signaling from most GPCRs is regulated by the beta-arrestin (ARRB) family of cytosolic multifunctional adaptor proteins, which mediate signal termination and endocytosis of GPCR-agonist complexes. The ubiquitously expressed non-visual beta-arrestin1 (ARRB1) and beta-arrestin2 (ARRB2) are highly similar but not functionally equivalent. The study demonstrated agonist-independent competitive interactions of ARRB1 and ARRB2 with MC1R. The effects of ARRBs were isoform specific; ARRB2 inhibited MC1R agonist-dependent cAMP production but not ERK activation, stimulated internalization and showed prolonged co-localization with the receptor in endocytic vesicles. By contrast, ARRB1 had no effect on internalization or functional coupling, but competed with ARRB2 for binding MC1R, which might increase signaling by displacement of inhibitory ARRB2. These data suggest a new mechanism of MC1R functional regulation based on the relative expression of ARRB isoforms, with possible activatory ARRB1-dependent effects arising from partial relief of inhibitory ARRB2-MC1R interactions (PMID: 23750009). The melanin pigment is a critical defense against ultraviolet radiation (UVR), and its production is mediated by the G(alpha)s-coupled melanocortin 1 receptor (MC1R). In HEMs, OPN3 acts as a negative regulator of melanin production by modulating the signaling of MC1R. OPN3 negatively regulates the cyclic adenosine monophosphate (cAMP) response evoked by MC1R via activation of the G(alpha)i subunit of G proteins, thus decreasing cellular melanin levels. OPN3 and MC1R colocalize at both the plasma membrane and in intracellular structures, and can form a physical complex. The results identify a function for OPN3 in the regulation of the melanogenic pathway in epidermal melanocytes (PMID: 31097585). 11074	MC4R-MRAP2 complex		Human	CHO cells	19329486	"MRAP and MRAP2 can interact with all 5 melanocortin receptors (MCRs). This interaction results in MC2R surface expression and signaling. In contrast, MRAP and MRAP2 can reduce MC1R, MC3R, MC4R, and MC5R responsiveness to [Nle4,D-Phe7]alpha-melanocyte-stimulating hormone (NDP-MSH) (PMID: 19329486).
The G protein-coupled receptor melanocortin-4 receptor (MC4R) and its associated protein melanocortin receptor-associated protein 2 (MRAP2) are essential for the regulation of food intake and body weight in humans. MC4R localizes and functions at the neuronal primary cilium, a microtubule-based organelle that senses and relays extracellular signals. The study demonstrates that MRAP2 is critical for the weight-regulating function of MC4R neurons and the ciliary localization of MC4R. The findings demonstrate that targeting of MC4R to neuronal primary cilia is essential for the control of long-term energy homeostasis and suggest that genetic disruption of MC4R ciliary localization may frequently underlie inherited forms of obesity (PMID: 36692018).
Studies in fish and avian species showed that MC4R becomes an ACTH receptor after interaction with the melanocortin receptor accessory protein 2 (MRAP2). Human MC4R behaves in a similar way through its interaction with MRAP2. Both proteins are coexpressed in the same hypothalamic neurons, providing an anatomical substrate and molecular mechanism for the central therapeutic actions of ACTH in the treatment of infantile spasms (PMID: 30652132).

11161	GPR39-HTR1A complex		Human	HEK-293S GnTi- cells	26365466	GPR39 is a class A G protein-coupled receptor involved in zinc binding and glucose homeostasis regulation, among other physiological processes. GPR39 was originally thought to be the receptor for obestatin peptide but this view has been challenged. However, activation of this receptor by zinc has been clearly established.  Zinc can alter receptor-receptor interactions and favor specific receptor interactions. The results suggest that zinc can modulate the formation of specific 5-HT1A-GPR39 and GalR1-5-HT1A-GPR39 heteroreceptor complexes under experimental conditions. The GPR39-5-HT1A heterocomplex has additive functionalities when compared to the monomeric-homomeric receptors upon receptor activation. In addition, the heterocomplex including also GalR1 shows a different behavior, upon exposure to the same agonists. Furthermore, these processes appear to be regulated by zinc. These findings provide a rationale for the antidepressive effect widely described for zinc because pro-depressive heterocomplexes are predominant at low zinc concentration levels.  (PMID: 26365466).		Studies suggest that low GPR39 expression, due to deficient zinc levels, is involved in major depressive disorder (PMID: 26365466). 11165	CRHR1-PDZK1 complex		Human	HEK 293 cells	25562428	The corticotropin-releasing factor receptor 1 (CRFR1) and serotonin 2A receptor (5-HT2AR) are linked to cellular mechanisms underlying stress anxiety and depression. Both receptors are members of the G protein-coupled receptor (GPCR) superfamily and encode class I PSD-95/DiscsLarge/Zona Occludens 1 (PDZ) binding motifs (-S/T-x-V/I/L) at the end of their carboxyl-terminal tails. The study identified PDZK1, also referred to as Na(+)/H(+) exchange regulatory cofactor 3 (NHERF3) as both a CRFR1- and 5-HT2AR-interacting protein. While PDZK1 interactions with CRFR1 are PDZ binding motif-dependent, PDZK1 associates with 5-HT2AR in a PDZ binding motif-independent manner and CRFR1 expression, but not 5-HT2AR expression, redistributes PDZK1 to the plasma membrane in PDZ binding motif-dependent manner. PDZK1, negatively regulates 5-HT2AR endocytosis and has no effect upon 5-HT2AR-mediated ERK1/2 phosphorylation. In contrast, PDZK1 overexpression does not affect CRFR1 endocytosis, but selectively increases CRFR1-stimulated ERK1/2 phosphorylation. Similar to what has been previously reported for PSD-95 and SAP97, PDZK1 positively influences 5-HT2AR-stimulated inositol phosphate formation, but does not contribute to the regulation of CRFR1-mediated cAMP signaling. Taken together, these results indicate that PDZK1 differentially regulates the signaling and trafficking of CRFR1 and 5-HT2AR via PDZ-dependent and -independent mechanisms, respectively (PMID: 25562428). 11197	CNR1-HTR2A complex	CB1R-5-HT2AR complex	Human	HEK-293T cells 	26158621	CB1R and 5-HT2AR form heteromers that are expressed and functionally active in specific brain regions involved in memory impairment (PMID: 26158621). 			Activation of cannabinoid CB1 receptors (CB1R) by delta9-tetrahydrocannabinol (THC) produces a variety of negative effects with major consequences in cannabis users that constitute important drawbacks for the use of cannabinoids as therapeutic agents. Behavioral studies carried out in mice lacking 5-HT2A receptors (5-HT2AR) revealed a remarkable 5-HT2AR-dependent dissociation in the beneficial antinociceptive effects of THC and its detrimental amnesic properties. Specific effects of THC such as memory deficits, anxiolytic-like effects, and social interaction are under the control of 5-HT2AR, but its acute hypolocomotor, hypothermic, anxiogenic, and antinociceptive effects are not. Functional data shows that costimulation of both receptors by agonists reduces cell signaling, antagonist binding to one receptor blocks signaling of the interacting receptor, and heteromer formation leads to a switch in G-protein coupling for 5-HT2AR from Gq to Gi proteins. Synthetic peptides with the sequence of transmembrane helices 5 and 6 of CB1R, fused to a cell-penetrating peptide, were able to disrupt receptor heteromerization in vivo, leading to a selective abrogation of memory impairments caused by exposure to THC. 11249	DRD1-DRD3 complex		Human	HEK- 293T cells	18644790	The formation of D(1)-D(3) receptor heteromers was demonstrated by fluorescence resonance energy transfer and bioluminescence resonance energy transfer techniques in transfected mammalian cells. 11251	D3 dopamine receptor	DRD3 homomer	Human	T-REx TM 293 Cells	22291025	Functional homomers and heteromers of dopamine D2L and D3 receptors co-exist at the cell surface (PMID: 22291025).			"Amisulpride, a benzamide derivative, is an antipsychotic drug with a pharmacological profile distinct from that of classical neuroleptics such as haloperidol and from that of another benzamide, remoxipride. Amisulpride has presynaptic D2/D3 dopamine receptor antagonist activity and limbic selectivity. The pharmacological profile of amisulpride, characterized by a preferential blockade of effects involving presynaptic mechanisms and limbic structures, may explain the clinical efficacy of this drug against both negative and positive symptoms of schizophrenia and its low propensity to produce extrapyramidal side effects (PMID: 8996184).
The D2/D3 agonist quinpirole, which induces receptor internalization in vitro, was administered at graded doses in non-human primates while imaging with simultaneous positron emission tomography (PET) and functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI). A pronounced temporal divergence between receptor occupancy and fMRI signal was observed: occupancy remained elevated while fMRI responded transiently. Analogous experiments with an D2/D3 antagonist (prochlorperazine) and a lower-affinity D2/D3 agonist (ropinirole) exhibited reduced temporal dissociation between occupancy and function, consistent with a mechanism of desensitization and internalization that depends upon drug efficacy and affinity (PMID: 26388148)." LGR6 binds and responds to R-spondins 1-3 with high affinity to enhance Wnt/beta-catenin signaling through increased LRP6 phosphorylation. Similar to LGR4 and LGR5, LGR6 is not coupled to heterotrimeric G proteins or to beta-arrestin following R-spondin stimulation. LGR6 was found as one of the novel genes mutated in colon cancer through total exon sequencing and its promoter region is hypermethylated in 20-50% of colon cancer cases. 11421	DRD1-NPFFR1 complex		Human	renal proximal tubule cells 	38965251	The kidney and brain play critical roles in the regulation of blood pressure. Neuropeptide FF (NPFF) and its receptors, NPFF-R1 and NPFF-R2, have been suggested to contribute to the pathogenesis of hypertension. Dopamine D1-like receptors colocalized and co-immunoprecipitated with NPFF-R1 and NPFF-R2 in human RPTCs. The increase in cAMP production in human RPTCs caused by fenoldopam, a D1-like receptor agonist, was attenuated by NPFF, indicating an antagonistic interaction between NPFF and D1-like receptors.  The renal subcapsular infusion of NPFF in C57BL/6 mice decreased renal sodium excretion and increased blood pressure. The NPFF-mediated increase in blood pressure was prevented by RF-9, an antagonist of NPFF receptors. Taken together, our findings suggest that autocrine NPFF and its receptors in the kidney regulate blood pressure, but the mechanisms remain to be determined (PMID: 38965251). Down-regulation of hippocampal orexin receptors (OXRs) and GPR103 was found particularly in the cornu ammonis (CA) subfield from AD patients suffering from early onset familial AD (EOFAD) and late onset familial AD (LOAD). Using an in vitro model the study demonstrates that this downregulation is due to to A-beta-plaque formation and tau hyper-phosphorylation (PMID: 26223541).
